- 🟡 Limit select distance and limit drag distance (human request, 2026-10-27; task `select-distance`; no matching open issue; merged at the human's request before their test, a test viewer left open for them): the Legacy Viewer's LimitSelectDistance / MaxSelectDistance and LimitDragDistance / MaxDragDistance (settings.xml; Build 1 preferences, 0.001 to 1024 m) become build settings, in a new "Distance limits" section of the construction settings under the ruler. The select limit governs every place the 128 m constant did: automatic deselection when the avatar walks away (LLSelectMgr::updateSelectionCenter), rectangle selection (llglsandbox.cpp), the edit stack under the cursor, the create and copy-selection tools and their preview (LLToolPlacer::raycastForNewObjPos), and the manipulator handles (LLManipTranslate / Rotate / Scale). The drag limit stops one move past its distance (LLManipTranslate::handleHover). Difference, at the human's request: LimitSelectDistance is off by default (the Legacy Viewer has it on at 128 m), so nothing is out of reach; the drag limit keeps the Legacy default (on, 48 m). Without the limit, the create tool's simulator ray reaches past a surface farther than the Legacy Viewer's 129 m. The Legacy Viewer's Advanced menu toggle has no place here: Aurora has no such menu. Full `scripts/check.ps1` green: 4,961 + 405 + 282 passed, zero failures; fmt, scripts and Clippy clean. Tests: far selection kept while unlimited and deselected past the set distance, range and defaults of both limits, edit stack under the cursor with and without the limit. French demo capture of the construction settings inspected.
  - ⬜ To verify (human): select, move and create past 128 m with the limit off; switch it on at a short distance and walk away from a selection.
- 🟡 Own avatar missing some outfit attachments after a login, Replace outfit not putting them back (task `outfit-attachments`, 2026-10-27; found during the cold-cache arrival measurements, the Legacy Viewer loses objects the same way now and then): at login the region puts back by itself one object per attachment point; the objects added on top are the viewer's to request (LLAppearanceMgr::updateAppearanceFromCOF, ATTACHMENT_ADD). Aurora requested them about 5 s after arriving, while the region was still putting its own back, all in one burst: "Attempt to rez an object failed" and, on a busy region, 18 of 38 objects missing with exactly one left per point. `world/outfit.rs` now waits for the region's restore to be quiet (4 s without a change, 12 s if nothing comes, 30 s at most), asks for the rest, asks again at once for an object the region takes off (its COF link kept, unlike a detach asked by the resident), and logs every step with item names; `session/attach_queue.rs` sends one RezMultipleAttachmentsFromInv at a time (LLAttachmentsMgr::requestAttachments), a limited number waiting for their object (8 at first, one more every 4 objects arrived up to 12, halved by a refusal, which also pauses it 5 s; four at a time made an outfit change on a busy region take two minutes), with a log line per run: on the grid, 18 requests 20 ms apart got the last 4 refused, and a refused item then stayed off for the session. Replace outfit keeps the Aurora bridge, as the Legacy Viewer puts it back into a replaced outfit. The COF sync after Replace outfit / Add no longer takes off a worn object whose link it cannot resolve yet and wears the objects it could not resolve once FetchItems brings them. Visible difference: the added objects appear a few seconds later than in the Legacy Viewer. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_OUTFIT_RESTORE=warm|cold`.
  - Validated by the human on AGNI on 2026-10-27, warm cache, crowded region: login 37 of 37 worn (the region put back 17 by itself, 20 requested, worn in 12 s), three outfit changes with no alert (22 objects worn in 6.5 s, 27 in 4.6 s), the Aurora bridge kept.
  - ⬜ To verify on the grid (human): a cold inventory cache login, launched outside Claude.

- 🟡 Freeze the world in photo mode ([#1154](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1154); task `photo-freeze-world`, 2026-10-27; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-27): a snowflake in the viewfinder's dock (fifth above the shutter), a "Freeze the world" tile in the quick menu (after Freeze frame) and a switch in the photo panel (under Freeze frame) hold every avatar, animation and moving thing still while the camera flies on; "World frozen" shows in the Full display. Rule from LLFloater360Capture::freezeWorld and the FreezeTime setting (indra/newview/llfloater360capture.cpp, pipeline.cpp, llviewerobjectlist.cpp): every character paused (LLCharacter::requestPause, here `Scene::pause_all_skeletons`, the motions resuming where they stopped), objects not moved (LLPipeline::updateMove), particles and clouds stopped. Aurora reuses the tiled photo's held instant (`snapshot::Hold`) for animations, avatar physics, flexible prims, water and portals, holds the animated textures' GPU clock too (`FrameParams::tex_anim_at`, the frame uniform's `anim_clock.zw`; now also held for photos in tiles), while the rez effects and the avatars' loading clouds go on, so what the moving camera finds still rezzes in, and keeps the objects that move, or that a report would move, at the place they were drawn (`ObjectStore::hold_poses`), our own avatar included; reports are still applied, so the world is current again on thaw. Never saved: leaving the photo mode thaws it. Demo word `frozen` (`AURORA_DEMO_SNAPSHOT=viewfinder-frozen`): captures at frames 700 and 900 differ by no pixel outside the hint banner (5,110 sampled pixels without the freeze).

- 🟡 Mesh import preview ignores BLEND ([#1157](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1157); [PR #1217](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1217); task `mesh-preview-ignore-blend`, 2026-10-27; validated by the human in the online test viewer): the Legacy Viewer's model preview draws with depth writes and blending disabled, while Aurora sent a glTF BLEND surface to a pass without depth writes even when its texture was fully opaque. The mesh import preview now draws BLEND surfaces as opaque, so their depth occludes later surfaces; the source material, material preview and Mask mode stay unchanged. Confirmation from the reporter remains pending; the original file's export format and alpha mode were not available for this investigation.
- 🟡 Rigged mesh layers z-fight in the upload preview ([#1157](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1157); [PR #1159](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/pull/1159); task `mesh-preview-layers`, 2026-10-27; validation handed to QA by the human): a mesh body whose layers share their positions (onion skins) showed a diamond z-fighting pattern in the rigged preview, clean in the Legacy Viewer. The Legacy Viewer keys skin weights by position (LLDAELoader / LLGLTFLoader `mSkinWeights[position]`, the last vertex written at a position wins; LLModel::getJointInfluences returns the first position in LLVector3 order within 1e-5 in normalized space), so coincident vertices of different layers skin identically; Aurora kept each source vertex's own list, and slightly different weights moved the layers apart by rounding. `skin::share_weights` now applies that rule in both loaders before `complete_weights`, which also fixes the weights sent at upload. Regressions `mesh_import_parity_dae_coincident_layers_share_the_last_source_weights` and `mesh_import_parity_near_positions_take_the_first_weights_within_epsilon`. A position grid (cells of twice the tolerance) and a parallel vertex pass keep it to about 130 ms for 600,000 vertices (dev build), once per load on the import worker. Synthetic demo check (`AURORA_DEMO_IMPORTS=mesh` with `AURORA_DEMO_IMPORT_FILE` on a red/blue two-layer rigged tube whose weights differ by 1e-4): before, red patches through the blue layer; after, a clean blue layer.
  - 🟡 QA: import a rigged layered mesh body (the reporter's case) with weights shown; the preview must match the Legacy Viewer's, with no diamond pattern between layers, and the uploaded body worn in-world must look the same.

- ✅ Enlarged mesh preview stretched in a wide window (human report, 2026-10-26; task `preview-aspect`; no issue; validated by the human in the demo on 2026-10-26, the enlarged preview stretched wide and tall): the 3D preview target clamped its width and its height to 1024 physical pixels each on its own, so past that size (a wide enlarged preview, or a high Windows scale) the texture had another shape than its rectangle and egui stretched the model to fill it. `preview::target_size` now scales both sides by the same factor, with a limit raised to 2048 pixels on the longest side so a large preview stays sharp. Applies to every 3D preview (mesh, material, shape editor, appearance hints). Unit test `large_preview_targets_keep_the_shape_of_their_rectangle`.

- 🟡 Bridge stopped after a teleport (human report, 2026-10-19; task `bridge-memory-recovery`; PR opened after a short grid check at the human's request): the grid showed a "Stack-Heap Collision" run-time error from the bridge script right after a teleport into a busy region, then every bridge request timed out and the viewer never recovered. A first grid test of the leaner 1.28 controller still showed only 5,378 bytes free at rest out of 65,536, mostly bytecode. Bridge 1.28 therefore splits the object into two scripts: the movement controller and `#Aurora Bridge Query` (`query.lsl`), which serves radar heights and script/object information with its own URL and token, announced in answer to the same probe; older bridges get only the missing script. Query bodies are read in place, avatar keys at a fixed stride, the altitude reply is built as text, and batches drop from 32 to 16 avatars. The controller's status carries `llGetFreeMemory` (Mono's lowest free memory), logged as `script memory low mark`. The viewer watches each script of a ready bridge: requests with no HTTP reply for 10 s query its running state. A stopped controller, or 90 s of controller silence, reinstalls the bridge through the Repair path (recompile, then detach/reattach save) with a chat notice, at most three times in ten minutes before leaving Repair to the user. A stopped query script is reinstalled the same way but never by silence alone, and at the limit it leaves Movelock working. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_MOVELOCK=halted`.
  - ✅ Lock indicator off by default (human request, 2026-10-19): "Show the lock indicator" now starts unticked for new accounts; the toolbar button still shows the lock state. Accounts that already saved the option keep their choice.
  - ✅ Grid check (2026-10-19, short session): on an existing bridge the viewer added only the missing query script, both 1.28 scripts compiled, the bridge reached Ready and the controller's low mark was 10,506 bytes free (5,378 before the split).
  - ⬜ To verify on Agni (not run on the grid yet): `query service ready` in the log; radar heights of distant avatars and script/object information through the query script; several teleports into a busy region with the radar open, without a Stack-Heap Collision, and the controller's low mark after them; Movelock hold and release; automatic reinstall after unticking Running on either script of the worn bridge.

- 🟡 Bridge after a region change (human report from a grid log, 2026-10-21; task `bridge-region-change`; PR opened after a short grid check at the human's request): grid logs showed `HTTP status 404` bridge warnings after crossings and teleports, and a full bridge reinstall (recompile, detach/reattach, about 16 s without Movelock) after 13 of 30 region changes. A region change sent a worn bridge back to the install path, which recompiled it whenever the attachment reached the new region before the script's new hello; and a region change less than 3 s after the bridge became ready replayed the old region's hello, whose URL had died with the move (404s, then 6–9 s without Movelock and an HTTP error in the Movelock window). Bridge 1.29: a moved bridge waits for its new hello in Handshake (probe and running check) and is reinstalled only after 30 s without one; only a hello that renewed a live endpoint is replayed across a region change; a controller 404 (the scripts never answer 404 themselves; the query script's "unavailable" body still means a missing object) is read as a dead URL: the viewer probes for the new one instead of showing an error, and logs it at info. Both scripts answer the first probe in a new region at once, and the controller announces its renewed URL once probed, even before its first command.

- 🟡 Inventory window frame rate (validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-16; tester report on 0.5.2, 2026-10-16: the frame rate drops for as long as the Inventory window stays open in a busy store, and recovers when it closes). Cause: the Inventory tab and the folder windows laid out every row of every open folder each frame (egui keeps the open folders between sessions, so one big folder opened once costs forever), and each inventory change rebuilt the sorted view with an ancestor walk and a set allocation per item. Fixed: the plain tree is a flat list of rows (`ui/inventory/rows.rs`), rebuilt only when the inventory, the sort or an open folder changes, and only the rows in sight are laid out, like the result tree of searches and tabs; open folders kept per window (the main window's with the UI layout, under a new key: folders opened before the update start closed once), guides and the row being renamed kept; the view rebuild dates folders and scopes trash, outfits and searches once per folder; the facts (worn, attachment points, names) are read only while a window or dialog shows them. Demo `AURORA_DEMO_INVENTORY=big[:<items>]` (30,000 items in ~3,000 folders, five levels, a 2,000 item folder open; options `recent`, `search=`, `toggle=`, `churn=`), dev build, `AURORA_FPS_LIMIT=120`, 5 alternated passes old / new: window open `u_inventory` 12.9 → 0.39 ms per frame, `ui` 13.5 → 0.84 ms, 72 → 120 fps (the cap), worst frame of the second 17.4 → 8.4 ms median and 54.8 → 8.6 ms at the 90th percentile; opening the window 50 ms → no slow frame; closed 0.11 → 0.06 ms; an inventory update with the window open 28 → 5.9 ms for its frame (3 passes). Recent (313 results) and a search (3,200 results) 0.3 ms. To verify on the grid: open the inventory in a busy place with `AURORA_PROFILE=1`, with big folders open.
  - ⬜ later: an inventory update still rebuilds the whole sorted view on the main thread (about 4 ms for 33,000 entries in the dev build): sort only the open folders' children and build the search entries when a search runs; a creator search clones every creator's name into the query each frame.

- 🟡 Fuzzing of the readers of untrusted data (human request of 2026-10-25, stability list point 1; task `fuzz-parsers`; PR authorised by the human on 2026-10-25; left: the first manual run of the Fuzz workflow after the merge): `fuzz/`, its own workspace outside the build. Thirteen targets cover what a resident or a simulator controls: JPEG2000 textures, mesh assets and sections, animations, LLSD (binary, notation, XML) and XML-RPC replies, GLTF materials and overrides, UDP packets with the object and terrain messages, compressed object updates and texture animations, texture entries, extra parameters and particle systems, prim shapes from their quantized parameters, sculpt maps of any size, terrain and wind patches, sounds, notecards, task inventories, gestures, wearables and base meshes. Seeds from our own encoders and shipped assets (a test checks every reader accepts them). `fuzz-local` (stable Rust, Windows) mutates them and reports panics, hangs over 10 s and allocations over 1 GB; the Fuzz workflow runs libFuzzer with AddressSanitizer every night on Linux, 10 minutes per target, corpus kept between runs. docs/TESTING.md "Fuzzing".
  - ⬜ Later: the readers inside the `aurora-viewer` binary crate (object cache files, scene parsers, bridge replies) cannot be called from `fuzz/`; move them into a library crate or fuzz them from tests.
  - ⬜ Upstream: symphonia-format-riff 0.6.1 multiplies two u16 WAV header fields for a log line (`wave/chunks.rs`); harmless in our builds (no overflow checks in dependencies), reported upstream.
  - Found and fixed: `aurora-assets` `j2k.rs` `calc_data_size_j2c` overflowed on a SIZ header claiming 2^32 - 1 on both sides.
  - 🟡 Found by the first workflow run (2026-10-25, task `fuzz-ci-findings`; PR authorised by the human on 2026-10-25; left for QA on the grid: textures still load normally, partial / progressive downloads included) and fixed: OpenJPEG allocates a tile-part's declared length (`Psot`, up to 4 GB) before reading it; a 163-byte texture asked for 1 GB. `j2k.rs` `bound_tile_parts` sets `Psot = 0` (until the end of the codestream) on a tile-part longer than the codestream and than twice the raw pixels plus 64 KB; partial downloads keep their lengths. The second run found the same allocation behind fill bytes that OpenJPEG skips to reach the SOT (1.6 GB): every SOT marker of the codestream is now checked, not only those the header's segment lengths lead to (task `j2k-sot-scan`, follows #1027; PR authorised by the human on 2026-10-25; same QA: textures still load normally, partial downloads included). The workflow builds with `cargo fuzz run -O` so that dependencies keep their wrapping arithmetic (symphonia's harmless overflow, upstream pdeljanov/Symphonia#598).

- ✅ Build speed on a PC shared by several agents (2026-10-14, chosen by the human). Compiler cache shared by the worktrees: sccache, installed by the Aurora tools, is wired by `new-task.ps1`, `check.ps1` and the repair through `<project folder>\.cargo\config.toml` (cache in `<project folder>\.sccache`, 10 GB, `AURORA_BUILD_CACHE_SIZE`), and unwired when it is uninstalled. Measured on a clean dev build of the viewer: a new worktree takes 71 % of its crates from the cache, about a third less processor time (sum of the units 1,131–1,413 s against 1,603–2,150 s), wall time 151–207 s against 176–207 s on a loaded PC; a worktree rebuilt after its `target\` was freed, 93 %. `check.ps1` takes one of two build slots (`AURORA_BUILD_SLOTS`) for clippy and the tests. Tests always on the whole workspace (`cargo test -p` alone builds the dependencies a second time). CI: a push to main no longer lints nor tests the commit the merge queue tested, it only rebuilds the Rust cache when its key changes. rust-lld measured and not adopted: incremental rebuild of the viewer, 6 alternated passes, median 13.2 s against 14.4 s with link.exe, within the noise (±10 s).

The window, its renderer and egui-winit's state are now dropped in `ApplicationHandler::exiting`, while the event loop still lives. Windows and X11 were not affected. Verified on Fedora (Wayland): three `AURORA_CAPTURE_EXIT` runs and a normal close by the human on 2026-10-27, exit code 0 and no core dump (every exit crashed before).

The Nightly workflow tags main every 12 hours (11:00 and 23:00 UTC: noon and midnight in France in winter) when it has an untagged commit (`v<next patch>-beta.<UTC date>.<n>`, `scripts/nightly-tag.ps1`, the newest stable tag's update policy carried over) and calls the Release workflow, which publishes it as a GitHub pre-release with symbols, policy and Linux archive; the ten newest betas are kept (`scripts/nightly-prune.ps1`). The updater's Beta channel takes the `-beta` pre-releases and the stable versions (a stable outranks the betas of its number); Stable, the website and the news ignore them. A beta build keeps checking for updates; back on Stable the beta stays until a newer stable (no downgrade); a channel change checks again at once. Betas are not signed (SignPath needs a manual approval per release). `scripts/test-nightly.ps1`, `AURORA_DEMO_UPDATE=beta`, `scripts/test-update.ps1 -Beta`.

## Network and protocol

- 🟡 Background inventory fetch (human request, 2026-10-26; task `inventory-background-fetch`; no issue; PR #1038; validated by the human on the grid on 2026-10-26): with an empty cache the inventory loaded only as folders were opened, one depth-0 AIS read per folder. Follow `LLInventoryModelBackgroundFetch::start` / `bulkFetchViaAis` / `onAISFolderCalback` / `onAISContentCalback` and `AISAPI::FetchCategorySubset`: from login on (after the cache, once the region has its capabilities), the root alone, then its folders by batches of 20 with their subtrees (`depth=50`), at most 19 reads in flight, a verify walk for what the depth limit or a failure left, and the recursive -> folder-and-content -> content fallback; the library through `LibraryAPIv3` (now requested). Marketplace listings stay with their window; folders the user opens keep their own reads and are never read twice. Deliberate difference: a root already read (the login's own read, or the cache) still loads its folders by batches instead of one recursive read each. Nested AIS replies are parsed off the main thread; folder sorting caches lowercase names. Grid, empty cache, 572 folders / 6,563 items: 6.0 s and 12 requests (one read per folder first measured 8.8 s / 65 requests). `inventory background fetch:` log line at the end; each read at debug level. Full `scripts/check.ps1` green: 5,365 passed, zero failures, 30 ignored.
  - ⬜ QA: a teleport and a region crossing while the fetch runs (the walk resumes on the new region's capabilities, `0 folders left` at the end).
  - ⬜ QA: a large inventory (tens of thousands of items): no hitch while replies are applied, no AIS throttling or 403 left unrecovered.
  - ⬜ QA: the library fully loaded through `LibraryAPIv3` (Library folders open already filled).
  - ⬜ QA: a second login with the full cache: only changed folders are read (few requests in the log line).
  - ⬜ QA: OpenSim or a grid without AIS: the `FetchInventoryDescendents2` fallback still walks the whole tree.
- 🟡 Linden Lab's viewer statistics (no issue; task `viewer-stats`; the Third Party Viewer Policy's clause on the viewer statistics packet; validated by the human on the grid on 2026-10-25: arrival and 5-minute reports accepted): Aurora asked for the `ViewerStats` capability and never posted to it. The session now posts send_viewer_stats' LLSD (indra/newview/llviewerstats.cpp) once the agent has arrived, every 5 minutes (SEND_STATS_PERIOD) and before the LogoutRequest (LLAppViewer::requestQuit), with the Legacy Viewer's fields and types: agent (start / run / foreground time, foreground fps, the frame time jitter of updateFrameStats, version "Aurora Viewer <x.y.z.n>", language, sim_fps, avatars in view, average ping, distance travelled, regions visited, resident memory, translation off), system (RAM, OS, CPU and its SSE levels, threads, the network adapter's address as `xx-xx-xx-xx-xx-xx` like send_viewer_stats (`machine_id::adapter_mac`, the adapter LLUUID::getNodeID picks, zeros without one) and the login's hashed `id0` as `serial_number`, both never logged, the GPU's name, vendor, driver, VRAM and largest texture, the API "Vulkan" where the Legacy Viewer gives OpenGL's version, GPU class -1 unknown, shader level 3 to 5 from shadows / AO), downloads (texture and mesh bytes; world and object 0, as the Legacy Viewer never adds to them), the message system's counters (zero-coded packets and savings in, out, send failures, lost, resent, failed resends, off-circuit, invalid), inventory usable, display name settings. The Legacy Viewer's own choices are kept: no preferences in the last report, no `ui` block, no setting to turn it off. A failed post is logged at debug level only, without the capability's URL; any 2xx answer counts as posted. The logged copies of the report show the adapter address and the serial as `(not logged)`, and the session id is added after logging. Quitting waits for the last report, 2 s at most and no longer than it takes (`NetClient::wait_viewer_stats`); Log out to the login screen keeps the network runtime, so it finishes on its own. Demo `AURORA_DEMO_VIEWER_STATS=1` logs the report once, nothing sent.
  - ⬜ QA: the logout report accepted (`viewer statistics posted to the simulator` at logout, with `RUST_LOG=info,aurora_net=debug`), after Log out and after quitting.
  - ⬜ QA: Linux (the adapter address, the reports accepted).
  - ⬜ QA: a long session (one report every 5 minutes, crossings and teleports counted in regions visited and distance).
  - ⬜ QA: no identifier in the logs (no MAC, serial or session id).
- 🟡 Login device ids like the official viewer (Third Party Viewer Policy, human's decision 2026-10-25; task `login-machine-id`; no issue; validated by the human on 2026-10-25): `mac` and `id0` were the md5 of a random UUID drawn at installation, so a reinstall gave a new device and machine bans could not hold. They are now computed as llHashedUniqueID and generateSerialNumber do (`machine_id.rs`): `mac` is the md5 of LLMachineID's six bytes (the Win32_ComputerSystemProduct UUID folded, else the Win32_OperatingSystem serial, else the NetBIOS adapter address, else 32 zeros; the first adapter address on Linux), `id0` the md5 of the C: volume serial (empty when unreadable) or of the longest /dev/disk/by-uuid name; `host_id` is sent empty, as the HostID setting. Computed once at startup off the UI thread; only the source kind is logged, never an identifier. Unlike the Legacy Viewer, the process-wide CoInitializeSecurity is not called (the proxy blanket is enough for these reads). On this PC, `mac` equals the System ID the Legacy Viewer logged, and `id0` the hash of the volume serial read independently. The random `machine_id` setting is gone.
  - ⬜ QA: a normal login on Windows and on Linux.
  - ⬜ QA: a VM or a machine with no network adapter falls back cleanly (login still works).
  - ⬜ QA: no identifier in the logs (only "login device ids computed: mac from …, id0 from …").
- 🟡 Quick login after a sudden close or a logout (#956; task `quick-relogin`; validated by the human on the grid on 2026-10-25: log out → immediate login shows the 10 s countdown): a login right after a crash, a killed viewer or a Log out to the same account landed in a region still logging the previous session out, and the avatar stayed frozen until the 90 s time-out. The login now tells the login server of a session that did not end cleanly (`last_exec_event` LAST_EXEC_UNKNOWN, `last_exec_duration`, `last_exec_session_id`, as the Legacy Viewer reads them from its exec marker; Aurora always sent 0 and no session id). A "presence" refusal (LoginFailedPendingLogout…) shows the grid's words and is tried again after 60 s, three times in a row at most. The AgentMovementComplete time-out sends a LogoutRequest before going back to the login screen, as STATE_AGENT_WAIT does. Per account (`login_wait.rs`, `last_sessions.json`), the last session's id, its sign of life every 15 s and its end: a login waits 10 s after a session the viewer saw end, 60 s after the last sign of life of one it never saw end, with a countdown in the connection progress (Escape cancels). Demo `AURORA_DEMO_LOGIN_WAIT=logout|sudden|refused`.
  - ⬜ QA: Escape during the countdown, then repeated immediate logins.
  - ⬜ QA: a killed viewer, then an immediate login (the 60 s wait from the last sign of life).
  - ⬜ QA: Escape, then an immediate login after a kill: does the grid now answer "presence" (the 60 s retry countdown) since it knows the previous session id?
  - ⬜ QA: two accounts: logging one out never holds the other back.
  - ⬜ QA: note the observed durations, to tune the 10 s / 60 s constants (`login_wait.rs`).

- 🟡 Stability: never lose a session to a blip (2026-10-17). The main simulator's circuit is dead after 100 s of silence as in the Legacy Viewer (llstartup.cpp `circuit_timeout`, was 60 s here: a laggy region or a short outage cut the session). From 5 s of silence a discreet pill under the top bar says the viewer waits for the region and counts the seconds (`ui/link_health.rs`; the Legacy Viewer gives no sign before "connection lost"). A lost link (silence, the main event queue given up after its 15 retries, the region closing the circuit, the arrival never completed) now says so and the next login goes back to the region and the spot the user was in (`uri:` start, same grid and account; a kick does not offer it): the Legacy Viewer goes back to the usual start location. A session that ends while the frame holds the window (the cursor locked by an orbit or mouselook) now gives the cursor back at the end of that frame instead of leaving it hidden and locked. `AURORA_DEMO_LINK=stall:<frame>[:<seconds>],lost:<frame>`. Validated in demo on 2026-10-18. Crash survey of the day: no panic in the local crash reports or the logs; the only freeze was the full video memory (fixed in #520); #494 (0.5.2, stopped in the background while Blender ran, no stack) points at a GPU device loss, see the ⬜ below.

  - ⬜ GPU device lost (driver reset when another application takes the GPU, #494): the device-lost callback now logs its reason and the crash report says so (task `crash-report-detail`, below); left: rebuild the renderer from the CPU-side caches instead of ending the session
- 🟡 A lost graphics card no longer ends the session with a Rust panic (task `gpu-device-lost`, #1237, PR #1275, 2026-10-28; validated in demo by the human on 2026-10-28; to verify on the grid: no new `handle_error_fatal` crash report after a driver reset; a tester's 8K photo, saved about a minute after a driver reset, panicked in wgpu's `Device::poll`, which treats a device loss found while waiting as fatal). The device-lost callback now sets a flag shared with the render thread (`aurora-render/src/device_lost.rs`): no read-back waits on the GPU any more (photos, captures, the click pick fail instead), the per-frame poll stops and no frame is built. At once a native box says the graphics card was lost, with what to try (driver, smaller photos, other programs, the safe graphics); its OK, or the window's close button, closes the viewer logged out. The session is reported as `GPU device lost` (`gpu-lost.txt`) and the next start offers the safe graphics. The Legacy Viewer has no notice. `AURORA_DEMO_GPU_LOST=<frame>`.
  - ⬜ A loss found by the very wait that hits it (the photo's own frame resets the driver) still panics inside wgpu on the render thread: the viewer then shows the same box and closes, the report stays a Rust panic
  - ⬜ Later: why the tester's driver reset (an 8K photo drawn in one pass? its video memory?): reason asked on #1237
- 🟡 A graphics card that stops answering no longer freezes the viewer (task `gpu-hang-recovery`, 2026-10-25; PR authorised by the human on 2026-10-25; grid checks by QA: on a PC where the viewer used to stay white or frozen after login, the window keeps answering and the "graphics card is not responding" box shows; No closes and logs out within a few seconds; the next start offers the safe graphics, "Use" switches to Potato, "Restore my graphics" puts the earlier settings back; a normal session shows no box and no card; a tester's window stayed white and frozen after login with no crash report: the main thread waited for the render thread without a bound). The renderer now waits at most 2 s for the render thread before building a frame (`Renderer::stalled_for`); while the GPU holds a frame no frame is built (the stores keep their writes, the interface's texture changes are carried over), the window keeps answering, sound and chat go on. After 6 s a native message box says the graphics card does not answer, with what to try, and asks to keep waiting (again a minute later) or to close (logged out, ended within a few seconds even if the render thread never comes back; the close button does the same, the exit prompt cannot be drawn); it goes away by itself when frames come again. The render thread's stack goes to the crash session (`gpu-stall.txt`), reported as `GPU not responding` (triage signature `gpu stall`). A session ended with the GPU in trouble (stall, device loss, frozen window) leaves a mark the next start consumes: the login screen offers the safe graphics (the Potato level, applied only on the user's click, the level's values kept aside in `graphics-before-safe.json` and offered back on the same card). The Legacy Viewer has a safe start chosen by hand (`--safe`, `LLFeatureManager::setSafe`) and no stall notice. `AURORA_DEMO_GPU_STALL`, `AURORA_DEMO_SAFE_GRAPHICS`.
  - ⬜ Later: after a device loss, rebuild the renderer from the CPU-side caches (stores' mirrors, decoded textures in the cache) instead of ending the session; then a stall that turns into a device loss could recover without a restart
- 🟡 Crash reports that can be acted on (task `crash-report-detail`, human request of 2026-10-25 after #978, #989 and #1001; demo `freeze` scenario run here, PR authorised by the human on 2026-10-25; left: a real report from a tester's freeze or crash on a release build: three "unexpected shutdown" reports with no stack and 17 identical "additional diagnostic" lines). A watchdog thread (`crash/watchdog.rs`) writes the session's sign of life every 5 s (`alive.txt`: time, last time the window answered, memory, and the state `app/crash_state.rs` notes every 2 s: screen, frame rate, window size, graphics preset, video memory, texture pressure, objects, avatars, regions). When Windows considers the window hung (`IsHungAppWindow`, the "Not responding" test; the Legacy Viewer's LLWatchdog ends the viewer itself, this one only observes), it suspends the main and render threads in turn and unwinds their stacks into `freeze.txt` (`native::write_thread_stack`: registers, `RtlLookupFunctionEntry` / `RtlVirtualUnwind` inside the suspended thread's stack, no allocation or lock while suspended). A session ended frozen is reported as `Freeze` with both stacks (the triage signs and names it `Crash: freeze in …`); a session whose watcher died with it gets its duration from the last sign of life and says whether Windows started again right after (system crash, power loss). The watcher hears Windows end the session (hidden window, `WM_ENDSESSION`): a shutdown is no longer reported. Reports also give the exit code's usual meaning, "GPU device lost" (new device-lost callback in aurora-render), a "Last state" table, and warnings as `-<s> s | level | Rust module | kind` with repeats folded. The crash window asks what the tester was doing (a few words needed before publishing, whatever the Preferences say: Always now opens straight on the report to publish instead of sending it by itself) and whether their graphics drivers are up to date (driver found shown beside it). `AURORA_DEMO_CRASH=freeze`.
  - 🟡 Blind crashes and silent thread deaths (task `crash-blind-spots`, human request of 2026-10-25; PR authorised by the human on 2026-10-25; grid checks by QA). Out of memory: the allocator (`allocator.rs`) hands a failed allocation to `native::out_of_memory`, which writes its size and stack to the pre-opened `oom.txt` without allocating, before the standard library aborts; a fast fail after it is reported as `Out of memory (N bytes)` with that stack (a handled failure, `try_reserve`, is not). Stack overflow: a vectored handler writes the stack as soon as the exception is raised (`Native exception 0xC00000FD`). Silent thread death: `crash/threads.rs` names the long-lived threads the session cannot do without (`aurora-net` runtime, `aurora-pages`, `aurora-trash`, `aurora-cache`, `aurora-texcache`, `aurora-chatlog`, `aurora-transcript`); their panic, which left the viewer running without them, now ends the session at the next frame, the window says "A part of the viewer stopped working" and the report adds `| Thread | … |`. Triage reads `Out of memory`. `AURORA_DEMO_CRASH=oom|overflow|thread`.
  - ⬜ Later: other fast fails (`abort`, a double panic, a security check) still have no stack: Windows Error Reporting local dumps; restart a dead non-critical thread instead of ending the session where that is safe
  - ⬜ sleep / resume: check that `Instant` keeps counting during sleep on Windows (QueryPerformanceCounter); if not, a long sleep would not end a dead circuit until 100 s after waking

- 🟡 Region without terrain or objects (Agni, 2026-10-09, login at Yikes: no RegionHandshake processed, only the ocean all the way; relaunching was enough). The simulator sends terrain and objects only after our RegionHandshakeReply, and Firestorm has neither retry nor timeout for this message (process_region_handshake): its only protection is the circuit. Aligned with LLMessageSystem::checkMessages: a reliable packet is acknowledged (and remembered against duplicates) only once decoded and processed, so the simulator resends an unreadable message instead of it being lost (before: acknowledged on receipt). Login like llstartup.cpp: UseCircuitCode resent every 5 s, 3 times (UseCircuitCodeTimeout / MaxRetries), CompleteAgentMovement only after its acknowledgement (before: sent anyway after 2 s), back to the login screen with the LoginPacketNeverReceived message if it never arrives. Log: decoding failures as warnings (message, region, sequence, limited per message), "region handshake from …" at each handshake, warning if the arrival region has not sent its own 10 s after AgentMovementComplete (counters of packets, failures, duplicates, dropped packets). No demo scenario (the demo does not go through the UDP circuit): unit tests of the circuit and of RegionHandshake decoding. Validated by the human on Agni on 2026-10-09 ("Test handshake-region": login at Yikes, TP to Tordangle and back, handshake of each region logged, no failure); as the original bug is random, to be watched in the logs (`no RegionHandshake`, `failed to decode`)
- ⬜ Later, to be decided: alert to the user when the arrival region has not sent its RegionHandshake (today, warning in the log only, 10 s after AgentMovementComplete): explain that the terrain and the objects will not arrive and offer to reconnect. Visible difference: Firestorm has neither alert nor retry for this message

- 🟡 Inventory and outfit after a border crossing (reported on Agni on 2026-10-16: after walking or flying into a neighbour, "This outfit's inventory is still loading" at the bottom of the inventory, nothing could be worn or attached any more). An outfit change refused while the new region had no capabilities set the current outfit and the outfit folders back to unloaded without asking for them again (`AppearanceUi::refresh`), and only the open Appearance window asked for them: every later change was refused for the rest of the session. Now, like the Legacy Viewer: a new seed drops the region's old capabilities until the new ones arrive (LLViewerRegion::setSeedCapability); a failed folder fetch is asked again once per change of region, then every failed folder when the agent's region gets its capabilities (LLInventoryModelBackgroundFetch waits for capabilitiesReceived, BGFolderHttpHandler::processFailure requeues); a refused outfit change asks again for the current outfit, the outfits and their missing link targets, so "still loading" lasts until they arrive. Unit tests of the crossing (fetch lost then asked again on the new capabilities) and of the refused change. To verify on Agni: walk and fly into a neighbour, then right after and a minute later wear an item, attach an object, take one off, open a folder of the inventory; the same after a teleport. Tried by the human on Agni on 2026-10-16: the inventory and wearing keep working after a region crossing
  - ✅ "The inventory server is not available yet" after a region change (#750, task `wear-after-region-change`): nothing could be worn or attached after a crossing or a teleport into a region already open as a neighbour. The first answer to a neighbour's seed lacks the inventory capabilities (74 against 77 for the agent's region in a grid log), and the crossing or EstablishAgentCommunication that makes it the agent's region repeats the same seed, which Aurora ignored: the region kept the neighbour's capabilities without `InventoryAPIv3`. Now, like LLViewerRegion::setSeedCapability, the same seed again is asked a second time beside the first request and the answer that grants more capabilities replaces the first (requestBaseCapabilitiesCompleteCoro); the event queue and the region features keep going. A new seed from EstablishAgentCommunication now drops the old capabilities too (it was only stored, and the region could stay without capabilities if the answer to the old seed was still on its way). Unit test `a_repeated_seed_is_asked_again_and_the_larger_answer_kept`; full `scripts/check.ps1` green (3,231 viewer tests). Validated by the human on Agni on 2026-10-21: after walking into a neighbour, a teleport to a neighbour and a teleport to a distant region, items are worn and attached; the log shows the second answer granting 77 capabilities where the neighbour's first had 74 (crossing and teleport to a neighbour), and 77 at once for the distant region

- 🟡 Running (SetAlwaysRun on a double tap), flying, crouching
  - 🟡 Stopping a flight keeps its momentum, as in Firestorm: Aurora sent a STOP (`AGENT_CONTROL_STOP`, the simulator's brake) with the end of the flight, so the avatar dropped straight down in both movement modes; Firestorm only clears the FLY flag (LLAgent::toggleFlying → setFlying, llagent.cpp) and the avatar falls on with the flight's speed. `App::toggle_fly` now does the same. With Aurora's movement the avatar then *coasts* (`own_motion.rs`, `Prediction::coasting`): while the simulator carries it faster than the keys ask, the lead goes from the flight's (3 m at 16 m/s) to the keys' at 3 m/s at most, instead of a walk's lead at once (on Agni the drawn speed fell from 15.8 to 4.9 m/s, then rushed at 27); what is left at the landing stays where it is drawn and fades. No speed is learned from reports in the air (vertical speed over 1 m/s, or a coast), nor a speed of the land over twice its usual one: the fall with momentum, forward held, had taught a walk of 11.9 m/s, and the walks after it ran 3 m ahead then dropped their lead. Unit test of the Agni case: no frame below 13 m/s before the landing (7.6 m/s without the coast). The flight's ramp starts at 0.5 s instead of none (Agni: from a hover, 90 % of the speed 0.55 s after the first report that moved): a flight of a moment while walking (fly pressed twice quickly) led by 2.9 m, the drawn avatar rushing at 14 m/s then standing still while the simulator caught up. Checked on Agni on 2026-10-16 (four sessions with `AURORA_OWN_MOTION_TRACE=1`): the end of a flight keeps its momentum, the drawn speed stays within 3 to 5 m/s of the simulator's (before: −11.7 to +12.1, up to 27.6 m/s), falls at rest and from a car roof are followed (0.8 m of glide at most), the learned walk stays 3.2 m/s. ⬜ To verify on Agni: the flight's ramp at a take-off and at a quick fly, fly.
  - 🟡 A session that ends flying logs in flying again (human request, 2026-10-16), the Legacy Viewer's `FlyingAtExit`: saved at logout, quit or disconnection (`LLAppViewer::disconnectViewer`, llappviewer.cpp), the FLY control set at login before the first AgentUpdate (`LLAgent::init`, llagent.cpp). Kept per account here (`world/flying_at_exit.rs`, the account's `flying_at_exit.json`; the Legacy Viewer keeps one value for the whole PC). A region that blocks flying now lands the avatar at its arrival and when its flags change (`process_agent_movement_complete`, `process_region_info`, llviewermessage.cpp; before, Aurora kept a flight there), and a login seated on an object stops the flight as before. The demo keeps no state. Unit tests: the saved state per account, the no-fly landing. ⬜ To verify on Agni: log out flying, log in again (flying), log out walking (walking), log in flying into a no-fly region (lands).

## Netcode audit — 2026-10-13

Audit requested by the human on 2026-10-13: what in the network code can cause freezes, lag, stutter or rubber-banding for a European user (about 200 ms of ping to Agni, simulators that lag now and then), and where Aurora can do better than Firestorm on the client side. Read: `crates/aurora-net` (circuit, session, capabilities, event queue, fetcher, object cache), the viewer side that drives it (`agent.rs`, `world/`, `scene/textures.rs`, `scene/meshes.rs`, `app.rs`, `ui/perf.rs`) and the matching Firestorm sources (`indra/llmessage`, `indra/llcorehttp`, `indra/newview`). Nothing here was measured on the grid by the audit: every figure marked "computed" is arithmetic from constants read in the code, and each item is one PR with its before / after measurement. The messages, capabilities and what the simulator expects do not change; only the client side does. A visible difference from Firestorm is said so in its item and is the human's decision.

> Today's grid logs (three sessions of 2026-10-13, RTX 4090, 500 to 1,500 fps): the `events` step costs 0.54 ms per frame at most on a one-second average, and the worst frames (0.4 to 1.5 s) are the first frame and waits outside the processor (`between`), not the network. But the logs hold no line about the network itself: no ping, loss, resend, queue age or input delay. Hence item 1 before anything else.

> Already better than Firestorm, to keep as it is: the network runs on its own runtime and is not tied to the frame rate (Firestorm reads the socket, flushes acks, resends and pings once per frame, with 20 ms or 400 messages per frame: `LLAppViewer::idleNetwork`, llappviewer.cpp); the UDP circuit and the seed capability start together at login (Firestorm waits for the capabilities and a decode loop before UseCircuitCode: llstartup.cpp STATE_SEED_CAP_GRANTED); cache misses are requested as each ObjectUpdateCached is read (Firestorm: once per frame); `Far` is sent in full on arrival (Firestorm: half the draw distance, then +10% per second: llviewermessage.cpp `send_agent_update`); downloads go through one priority queue with time-boxed results on the main thread (llcorehttp is first in, first out and its texture results are picked up by a sweep that takes 20 frames or more to go round: `LLViewerTextureList::updateImagesFetchTextures`); a disk cache hit never touches the network; our avatar's extrapolation tapers from 2 s to 3 s on a silent circuit (Firestorm hands `InterpolationTime` and `InterpolationPhaseOut` to the wrong setters, llviewerobjectlist.cpp `setPhaseOutUpdateInterpolationTime( interp_time )`: full speed for 3 s, then a dead stop).

Suggested order (1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11, 13 and 15 are done): 17 and 19, then the rest; 3 and 4 are the ones that change what the user feels most and need the human's decision.

**Measure first**

- ✅ **1. Network line in the log and in the Performance window.** Nothing told how late an input leaves, how old an update is when it is applied, or how long the UDP loop stalls. Done: with `AURORA_PROFILE=1`, one `net summary` line per second of a grid session next to `perf summary` (`net_profile.rs`; fields in docs/TESTING.md, "Profiling › Network"): ping, last and smoothed; packets and throughput in / out; reliable packets resent, given up, duplicates, unacked; sequence numbers skipped by the simulators and packets that came late (their difference is what never arrived); longest time the session loop spent on one wake-up (`loop_max`); events applied by the main thread, most left waiting at the end of a frame and longest wait since the network sent them (each event now leaves the session with its time); AgentUpdates sent and longest delay between a change of the control flags and the AgentUpdate that carried it (`NetClient::set_controls`, not counted during a teleport); corrections of our avatar: simulator reports more than 0.5 m from the extrapolated position, like Firestorm's `AGENT_POSITION_SNAP`, and the largest distance, moves of more than 10 m left out; asset requests in flight, queued, finished, failed and retried, and one line per asset host with the HTTP version it answers in. Performance › Network shows the input delay (last one measured), the corrections of the session, the loop pause and the event wait of the last second, without the variable. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_PERF=network` opens the window on that section (the demo has no circuit: the rows are there, their values empty). `check.ps1` green (1,818 tests passed, 23 ignored); unit tests of the counters, of the sequence gaps, of the corrections and of the line. Not counted: new HTTP connections (the HTTP client does not report them). Window and lines validated by the human on Agni on 2026-10-13 ("Test net-summary").
  - First reference, Agni, 2026-10-13: one busy region, 92 s of walking, no teleport, medians of the `net summary` lines. Ping 202 ms (smoothed 234). Input delay 94 ms, 123 ms at the 95th percentile, 125 ms at most, over the 59 seconds that had a key change: what item 2 computed, and close to half the ping added on top of it. 6 corrections of our avatar, the largest 0.96 m. No resend, duplicate or sequence gap. Session loop: 0.11 ms, 3.8 ms on arrival (no cache write in so short a session: item 8 is not measured yet). Event wait 8 ms, 15 ms at the 95th percentile, the channel empty at the end of every frame. Both asset hosts answer in HTTP/1.1; 104 of the 637 asset requests failed, the ones listed in the log with a 403.
  - ⬜ To do on Agni by the human, to complete the reference: a teleport there and back, a stay of more than two minutes in a dense region (object cache write) and a quiet place, with `AURORA_PROFILE=1`.
  - ⬜ Later, simulated link in demo (`AURORA_DEMO_NET_LAG=<ms>[,<jitter ms>[,<loss %>]]`) that delays and drops the updates of the offline simulator, so that items 3, 4, 5 and 6 can be developed and captured without a grid (the demo does not go through the UDP circuit; `AURORA_DEMO_AGENT_JITTER` already shakes the agent).

**Input latency and our own avatar**

- ✅ **2. Control changes sent at once (alignment with Firestorm).** A key press or release was written to a shared structure that the session read on a 25 ms tick, and a change was only sent when 100 ms had passed since the last AgentUpdate: while walking, turning or moving the camera the updates already flowed at 10 per second, so a press or a release waited up to 125 ms (measured on Agni: 94 ms at the median on a 202 ms ping, item 1); a press and its release inside one window were never sent, and a release sent late made the avatar overshoot. Fixed like `send_agent_update` (llviewermessage.cpp; `agent_update.rs`): any change of the control flags leaves at once and is confirmed by one more update (`control_flags_follow_up`); camera position past 0.01 m, camera axis past 0.2 × π / 360, body rotation past a dot of 0.9997, head rotation past 0.9997 at once or, down to 0.99999, once it has waited (threshold growing over 0.5 s), render state and flags: 125 updates a second at most (`MAX_AGENT_UPDATES_PER_SECOND`); one update a second keeps the agent alive. The viewer hands the session each change of the flags, in order, and whatever moved past those thresholds (`NetClient::set_controls` → `NetCommand::AgentControls`), so the session wakes for it instead of waiting for its tick, and a key tapped between two ticks is sent as two updates; the tick keeps the keep-alive, the follow-up and the head band. The draw distance no longer causes an update of its own: it travels with the next one, as in Firestorm. `check.ps1` green (1,833 tests passed, 23 ignored); tests of the rule: key at once and confirmed, tap shorter than the limit, thresholds, 125 a second for a camera moving at 1,000 frames a second, head band, keep-alive and forced update. Validated by the human on Agni on 2026-10-13 ("Test agent-update-now", 86 s of walking, stops, turns and short taps): input delay 0.0 ms in each of the 38 seconds that had a key change (before: 94 ms median, 125 at most), AgentUpdates 27 a second at the median and 121 at most (before: 10), no resend, no sequence gap.
- 🟡 **3. Movement prediction of our own avatar (visible difference from Firestorm: a choice in Preferences › Aurora › Movement, Firestorm's by default until the human has tried it on Agni, marked experimental meanwhile by a warning triangle and its tooltip).** Like Firestorm, Aurora moved our avatar only when the simulator's update came back (`LLViewerObject::processUpdateMessage`): at 200 ms of ping it started and stopped a fifth of a second after the key. Done (`own_motion.rs`, `agent.rs`, `app/own_motion.rs`): with "Instant", the drawn avatar is the simulator's extrapolated position plus a lead, the motion the keys asked for over the last delay (round trip + the simulator's step), which is what the simulator has not played yet since it plays our inputs that much later. The intent comes from the control flags actually sent (keys and autopilot), the body's heading and the run state; jumps and crouching on the spot are not predicted. The lead comes from the keys alone, so it cannot drift: once they are released it drains in one delay while the simulator plays the end of the motion. The drawn avatar glides to that aim (a critically damped follow of 0.08 s, about Firestorm's drawable damping), so a stop eases out over about 0.15 s instead of halting in one frame; after a release it only slows down (a simulator that stops a physics step later than the lead expected is caught up at the speed the avatar had), a simulator that stops a step sooner leaves the avatar where it is drawn, and a correction under 0.15 m at rest waits for the next move to fade (the human's demo trial of 2026-10-16 felt a jolt at each stop: the avatar halted in one frame, then moved 5 cm on or back when the simulator's stop arrived a frame apart from the lead's; measured before: 3.2 m/s lost in one frame and a 5 cm pop 200 ms later, 0.24 m of pull-back on the first stop; after: at most 0.5 m/s lost per 16 ms, no rise, no pull-back, at 60 and 500 fps). The walk goes on until the drawn avatar is under 0.5 m/s. When the simulator does not follow (a wall, a freeze, a push: its velocity under half the asked one once it should be moving), the lead fades (0.1 s half-life) and the server's motion alone is drawn until the keys change; three such failures within 10 s suspend it for 5 s. Never seated (on an object, a vehicle as passenger or driver, a prim at rest, the ground), during a teleport or before the arrival: a change of parent drops the lead and the first frame standing starts from the simulator's position. Seated, Firestorm's keys orbit the camera or go to the vehicle's script (`key_bindings.xml` <sitting>, `camera_move_forward_sitting`, llviewerinput.cpp): the flags still leave, the drawn avatar is where its seat carries it. On the land the lead follows the slope and stays in the known regions. The body turns with the drawn velocity. Calibration instead of step (a): the speeds per mode (walk, run, crouch, nudge, fly, climb), the ramps (start and stop) and the delay beyond the round trip are learned from the simulator's reports, seeded with walk 3.2, run 5.13, fly 16 m/s (crouch, nudge, climb, ramps and delay are guesses), and logged (`own motion learned: …`, `lead_max=` in `net summary`). Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_LINK=<ping>[,jitter=][,aurora|firestorm][,vehicle]` (`demo_link.rs`), a stand-in simulator behind a simulated link; with 200 ms and `AURORA_DEMO_KEY=up:pulse`: Firestorm's movement starts 250 to 317 ms after the press and stops 500 ms and 0.9 m after the release, Aurora's starts within one frame and stops within one frame, 0.00 to 0.01 m on (the same with 40 ms of jitter). `check.ps1` green; unit tests of the intent, the lead (round trip, wall, push, suspension, reset), the calibration, the seated cases (passenger, driver, prim at rest, ground, standing up) and the slow corrections. To verify on Agni, side by side with Firestorm's: walk, run, fly, stop and turn on flat land and on slopes; walking into a wall and being pushed; sitting on a vehicle and on a chair and standing up; a region crossing on foot; the `own motion learned` values (real speeds, ramps and delay) to replace the guesses. The default is the human's choice once tried.
- 🟡 **4. Softer corrections of our avatar and its animations with the keys (visible difference from Firestorm, with 3).** With Aurora's movement, a correction of 0.5 to 3 m fades with a 0.25 s half-life instead of Firestorm's 0.06 s (`OBJECT_DAMPING_TIME`, `LLDrawable::updateXform`), beyond 3 m with 0.06 s, beyond 10 m it snaps as before; the gap rides on the extrapolation instead of the drawable chasing the moving position (as `world/motion.rs` already does for the other objects), so a walking avatar is not drawn late, and the camera follows the drawn position. The corrections above 0.5 m are still counted (`AGENT_POSITION_SNAP`). Checked: Firestorm starts our walk, run and fly only on the simulator's AvatarAnimation (`process_avatar_animation`, llviewermessage.cpp; `LLVOAvatar::processAnimationStateChanges`). With Aurora's movement they start with the key and stop with its release (`own_motion::Locomotion`): the simulator's stock motion the keys will bring (walk, run, crouchwalk, fly, hover up / down) replaces the stand at once, the simulator's signal takes over keeping the cycle's start, and on a release the moving motions are hidden until the simulator stops them (a stand or a hover in their place); a start or stop the simulator does not confirm within the round trip + 0.6 s is dropped. The AO sees the same signals, so its overrides follow the keys too. Firestorm's movement: everything as before (the setting off, or offline without the simulated link). To verify on Agni with 3: no foot sliding at a stop, no double start of the walk, the AO's walk and stand following.
  - 🟡 A late stop no longer brings the walk back (human report on Agni, 2026-10-16: "latences d'arrêt d'animation violentes" with Aurora's movement): the local stop waited a fixed time for the simulator's own (the ping and 0.6 s, after the glide), then gave up, and when the simulator's walk signal came later (a busy simulator, a slow link: up to 364 ms of ping in that session) the walk came back for a moment, and the AO's with it, before the simulator's stop. Now the local stop is kept past that wait while the simulator does not report our avatar moving, 3 s at most (`Locomotion::overlay`, `HOLD`); a report of motion (pushed, a key lost) gives the simulator's walk back after the wait as before. The same for a start: the local walk is kept past the wait while the drawn avatar moves (it stopped under a moving avatar, feet sliding, when the simulator's walk signal was late). Reproduced in demo with `AURORA_DEMO_LINK=350,aurora,trace,stoplag=800` (new: the stand-in keeps its walk signal that long once stopped) and `AURORA_DEMO_KEY=up:pulse`: the walk came back 1.1 s after each release; now none, with `stoplag=800` or `1500`. ⬜ To verify on Agni: stops with an AO, in a busy region.
  - 🟡 A fall without keys is followed (human report on Agni, 2026-10-16: "quand j'arrête de voler ça me repositionne un peu violent"): after a release the drawn avatar only slows down (`ease_out`), and an avatar nearly at rest kept its nearly zero speed, so when the simulator dropped it at the end of a flight it hung in the air (5.8 m above the simulator's avatar in the trace) until the next key, then fell 6 m in a few frames. The rule now holds horizontally and for the last 0.5 m of a stop only; the height always glides to the simulator's (fall, landing, take-off), and a correction left at rest waits for the next move horizontally only (a landing left the feet 0.14 m in the ground). Grid trace: `AURORA_OWN_MOTION_TRACE=1` (new, docs/TESTING.md). Unit test of the Agni case (hovering, no key, a 5.8 m fall): 5.9 m hung before, now the glide's 0.8 m behind at 10 m/s and on the ground at the end. ⬜ To verify on Agni: stop flying at rest and while moving, jump, walk off a ledge.
  - ⬜ Later: the lead ignores the region's time dilation. A busy simulator plays our motion slower in real time (at a dilation of 0.5 a walk covers 1.6 m/s; the simulator's reports are extrapolated with it, as in Firestorm, `predict_agent`), but the lead assumes full speed: about twice too far ahead there, and with a strong dilation `check_follow` would take it for a simulator that does not follow and drop the lead at once. Scale the lead's motion by the main region's dilation (`SimulatorMotion::time_dilation`), keep the calibration in simulator time (the reports' velocities), and write the dilation in `net summary` and the `AURORA_OWN_MOTION_TRACE` line; verify on Agni in a busy region (an event, a crowded club). The ping per region is already followed (the main circuit's smoothed round trip, measured every 5 s).

**Other avatars and moving objects**

- ✅ **5. Extrapolation and smoothing of the others (alignment with Firestorm, then better).** Everything that is not our avatar was drawn by `Object::predicted`: position + velocity × time, with the time cut at 0.6 s, no time dilation, and each update applied as it is. An avatar or a vehicle on a steady course froze 0.6 s after its last update, although the simulator deliberately sends nothing while the object follows the path it announced (`LLViewerObject::interpolateLinearMotion`), then jumped at the next one; a spinning object (llTargetOmega) stopped for good after 0.6 s; every correction was a snap. Fixed (`world/motion.rs`): an object follows its reported velocity, acceleration and spin for as long as the circuit of its region lives, with Firestorm's physics step (the closed form of its per-frame sum, the same at any frame rate; the angle of a spin keeps its precision for days). Time is the simulator's: each region has a clock (`ObjectStore::motion_time`, advanced by `World::advance_motion` from the dilation and the last packet of every simulator, `NetStats::simulators`) that runs at the region's time dilation, slows down after 2 s of silence of its circuit and stops at 3 s; an object then stays where it was and goes on when the circuit is back. A report that puts an object elsewhere than where it was drawn opens a gap that fades with Firestorm's half-life of 0.06 s, in position and rotation, snapping beyond 10 m (`Correction`, the damping of `LLDrawable::updateXform`); while it fades the object counts as moving for the scene, then is placed for good. Not corrected: a new object, a change of parent (sitting, standing up), an object that came from another region, and a pose written locally since the report (a drag in the build tools). An extrapolated avatar stays half its height above the land. **Better than Firestorm, deliberately:** the fading also applies to objects in motion (Firestorm only damps avatars and objects whose velocity is zero, `LLViewerObject::updateDrawable`, so its physical objects and vehicles snap), and it rides on the extrapolation instead of chasing it, so a moving object is not drawn late. `check.ps1` green (1,863 tests passed, 23 ignored); tests of the extrapolation (steady course, sum of Firestorm's steps at 10 / 45 / 600 frames a second, spin over days), of the clock, of the correction (half-life, shortest turn, too small / too far) and of the store (clock per region, border crossing, fading and its end, local write, change of parent). Validated by the human on Agni on 2026-10-13 ("Test others-motion", 206 s, two regions, one teleport): walking avatars, vehicles and physical objects, spinning objects, scripted doors, build tools drag, sitting and standing up, nothing to report; `sync` 0.10 ms per frame at the median, 0.27 at the 95th percentile.
  - ⬜ Later: stop an extrapolated object at the edge of a region that has no neighbour there (Firestorm's clip in `interpolateLinearMotion`; our avatar already has it, `clip_to_visible_regions`), and a demo scenario with sparse updates once the simulated link of item 1 exists.
- 🟡 **6. Update times taken at reception.** `update_time` and `last_server` were `Instant::now()` when the main thread applied the event, after its wait in the event channel (Firestorm takes the frame time too: `mLastInterpUpdateSecs`), so every update shifted a moving object by speed × wait. Done: each event already left the session with the time it was sent, right after the datagram was read and decoded; `World::apply_received` hands it to the object updates: with Aurora's movement our avatar's report starts its extrapolation from that moment (`AgentState::on_server_update_at`; with Firestorm's movement it keeps the frame time, as on Firestorm and before), and an object's motion is stamped on its region's clock at that moment (`ObjectStore::report_clock`: the clock, plus or minus the time from its last tick at the region's rate), its correction measured against where it was drawn for that moment. Events applied without a time (the demo, the tests) keep the clock as it is. The objects and the other avatars take the reading time whatever the movement setting: it extends item 5, which is already outside the toggle and deliberately better than Firestorm. Tests of the stamping (before and after the tick, time dilation). To verify on Agni: other avatars walking and vehicles driving past look as smooth as before or smoother, with no shift at each update in a busy region. Later, to decide with the measurements of item 1: compensation by half the ping (Firestorm's `PingInterpolate`, off by default) or a short interpolation buffer for the other avatars.

**UDP circuit when the link or the simulator lags**

- ✅ **7. Receive and send buffers of the UDP socket (alignment with Firestorm).** The socket was bound with the system's sizes (64 KiB on Windows). On arrival the main region and up to eight neighbours send their objects at once: whatever does not fit while the loop is busy is lost, resent a second later when it was reliable, gone for the unreliable position updates (jump at the next one). Done: 800,000 bytes in reception and 200,000 in emission, as Firestorm's `start_net` (`RECEIVE_BUFFER_SIZE`, `SEND_BUFFER_SIZE`, llmessage/net.cpp), through `socket2` (already there as a dependency of tokio); the sizes obtained are logged once per session (`udp socket buffers: …`, docs/TESTING.md, "Profiling › Network"). A system may grant less (Linux caps at `net.core.rmem_max`); a refusal is a warning and the session goes on. Test: the socket gets what is asked for on Windows, never less than its default elsewhere. `check.ps1` green (1,870 tests passed, 24 ignored). Verified on Agni by the human on 2026-10-13 ("Test udp-buffers-cache-io", two sessions): `receive 800000 bytes (system default 65536), send 200000 bytes (system default 65536)`. Its effect on losses does not show in these sessions: the loop was never busy when packets came in numbers, and the sessions before had no sequence gap either; the 3 and 12 gaps of the two sessions fell in seconds where the loop stayed under 0.2 ms, so they are losses on the link.
- 🟡 **8. No file work on the session loop.** The object cache of a region was read in the RegionHandshake handler, and every changed cache was serialised and written every 120 s, when its simulator went and at the end, all on the task that reads the socket: during that time nothing was received, acknowledged or answered. Measured on this PC (default profile, SSD, file already in the system's cache): 3.3 ms to read and 3.1 ms to write a cache of 12,827 objects (3.9 MiB), 13.8 and 13.1 ms for a full one of 60,000 (18 MiB), for each region — up to nine in the same tick — and more on a cold or slow disk. Done (`session/object_cache.rs`, `objcache.rs`): the file is read by a blocking task and RegionHandshakeReply leaves when it is loaded, with the same flags as before (its "cache empty" bit needs the cache); a handshake sent again meanwhile does not read twice, a simulator that left gets nothing. The payloads are shared, so the loop only takes a snapshot of a cache that changed (0.15 ms for 12,827 objects, 1.1 ms for 60,000) and one writer writes the snapshots in the order they were taken: two writes of one region never overlap and the latest wins. A write that failed is taken again at the next period; the end of the session waits for the writer, so that the next one reads up-to-date files; clearing the cache in Preferences also drops what was being read or waited for the writer. Firestorm reads the cache on its main thread, in the same handler (`LLViewerRegion::unpackRegionHandshake` → `loadObjectCache`). Log, without any variable: `object cache for <region>: … entries, read in … ms` and `object cache written: … objects, … KiB in … ms`. Tests: content and order of the snapshots, failed write, reply to the handshake held until the cache is read (cached region, new region, no region id, repeated handshake, simulator gone), writes in order and read back, cleared cache. `check.ps1` green (1,870 tests passed, 24 ignored). Human trial on Agni on 2026-10-13 ("Test udp-buffers-cache-io", 213 s with a teleport there and back, then a new login of 66 s): objects appear as before on login, after both teleports and after the new login, which read the file the first session wrote at its end; four reads of about 12,800 objects in 3.1 to 4.0 ms, the reply to the handshake leaving 3 to 4 ms after it; one periodic write and one at the end, 3.1 and 3.3 ms; `loop_max` stays under 0.45 ms during both logins (5 to 6 ms in the second of the handshake before).
  - ⬜ To verify on Agni: an arrival in a region that has neighbours (several caches read at once, the cache of a neighbour written when it is left: both regions of the trial stood alone), and Preferences › clear the cache during a session.
  - ⬜ Later: the loop still pauses 5 to 21 ms now and then during the six seconds that follow a teleport (both teleports of the trial, neither login), in seconds where the main thread also runs frames of 50 to 70 ms. It is not file work, and not the decoding of cache hits (1 µs per object, measured on a local cache of 12,955 objects). To find out: name in `net summary` which wake-up held the loop (datagram, tick, command, capability) and whether its thread was working or waiting for a processor while the decode workers take every core.
- 🟡 **9. Seed capability: a failure must not be final.** `resolve_seed` tries 4 times in about 5 s, then the viewer shows "capabilities unavailable" and never asks again (`caps_requested` stays set in `request_caps` / `on_caps`): on a simulator that lags at the wrong moment the region stays without textures, inventory or teleports until a relog. Firestorm tries 30 times (`MAX_CAP_REQUEST_ATTEMPTS`, llviewerregion.cpp). Capability requests also have no overall timeout (`caps_http` only has a connection timeout): one that hangs never returns. To do: retries up to Firestorm's count with a capped delay and some jitter, a timeout on every capability request, the alert only when everything failed, and a new attempt on the next region change. **Done on 2026-10-13** (`caps::resolve_seed`, `SeedRetry::FIRESTORM`): the seed is asked 31 times like `LLViewerRegionImpl::requestBaseCapabilitiesCoro` (more than `MAX_CAP_REQUEST_ATTEMPTS` failures give the region up), each request given the 30 s of llcorehttp, the next one 1, 2, 4 then 5 s later (its `HTTP_RETRY_BACKOFF_MIN` / `MAX_DEFAULT`) with up to a fifth more at random; a reply that is not a map counts as a failure, as Firestorm's "malformed response". The requests stop when the session ends; one request per simulator, a new seed takes the place of the old and the answer to a previous seed is ignored (`mHttpResponderID`). The alert comes only once every attempt failed, for the agent's region, and the seed is asked again when that region is entered again. Six tests (spacing, a seed that answers at the fourth request, one given up after every attempt or when no longer wanted, a request left without reply, the session's handling of a stale answer and of a failure). Validated by the human on Agni on 2026-10-13 for the ordinary case: a login and a teleport, 54 capabilities each time at the first request, 0.3 s after the arrival. 🟡 because the retries themselves cannot be provoked on the grid: the log says `seed capability answered at attempt n` when they served.
  - ⬜ Later: a timeout on the other capability requests (`caps::request_llsd` has none; the event queue has its own).
- 🟡 **10. Event queue kept alive in a quiet place, errors like Firestorm.** The failure counter of the loop was only reset by a reply that carried events, and a long poll that ends without one is cut as a transport error about once a minute ("event queue error: error sending request", present in every grid log). In a place where nothing happens the errors added up, and at the 21st the loop gave up for good ("event queue for … giving up", seen in the log of a long session of 2026-10-09 after twenty-odd minutes of errors a minute apart): from then on no TeleportFinish, no chat session, no parcel event reached the viewer until a relog. Statuses 499 to 504 were also polled again after 100 ms whatever the time the request took, without counting: a simulator answering an error at once received 10 requests per second. Fixed like `LLEventPollImpl::eventPollCoro` (lleventpoll.cpp; `after_poll` in `caps.rs`): a poll the simulator held 10 s or more (`MIN_SECONDS_PASSED`) and that ended without an event is "no event" and forgets the errors, whatever ended it — our timeout, a 499 / 500 / 502 / 503 / 504, or the held connection being cut, which is how that end shows through our HTTP client; anything sooner, and any other status, is an error: wait 1 s + 3 s per error already counted, give up after 15 in a row (about 5 minutes of continuous failure); a 404 closes the queue. A reply without an id keeps the previous acknowledgement. When the queue of the agent's region gives up, the session ends with the "connection lost" message, as Firestorm's forced disconnect, instead of staying open without teleports; a neighbour only loses its own events (warning in the log). `net summary` gains `event_queue idle= errors=` (docs/TESTING.md). `check.ps1` green; tests of the rule (a quiet place for hours, back-off and give-up, recovery, closed queue), of the loop against a local server (events, acknowledgements across an error) and of the lost queue (agent's region, neighbour, queue replaced since). Unchanged: our 75 s timeout (Firestorm: 30 s). Human trial on Agni on 2026-10-13 ("Test event-queue-errors"): 5 min 25 s alone in a skybox, 10 idle polls (two a minute), no error, where the previous code counted one about once a minute.

One round trip to the first pixels.** The first request of a texture was a fixed 16 KiB (`INITIAL_BYTES`); when that was not enough for the wanted level, the data was not decoded and a second range was asked: two round trips and the queue before anything but grey. It also left before the size of the texture on screen was known (that size was noted when the turn of its object came, up to 30 frames later): at the same rank as every other texture, and its level computed for a file of 512 pixels until the next pass, one level too fine for a 1024 texture (four times the pixels decoded, four times the bytes asked). Firestorm also takes two steps (600 bytes, then the range of the level: `FIRST_PACKET_SIZE`, LLTextureFetchWorker::doWork). Done (`scene/textures.rs`): (a) an object whose faces were just built has the size of its textures on screen noted in the same frame (`Scene::fresh_usage`), so the first request of a texture in view leaves at the rank that size gives it; (b) that request asks what a 1024 texture needs to show that many pixels (`first_bytes`: 16 KiB up to 128 pixels, 44.6 KiB up to 256, 172.6 KiB beyond, never the whole file before its size is known), so one reply is enough for most; (c) when the file tells its size, from the first bytes or from the disk cache, the level wanted is computed again for that size (`Entry::want_for_its_size`); (d) when the bytes held still do not reach the level wanted but hold a coarser one, that one is decoded and shown while the rest is asked (`Entry::holds_first_pixels`). **Better than Firestorm, deliberately:** it shows nothing of a texture before its second reply. Measured in demo, 400 textures of a local cache downloaded from a local server at 200 ms a request (`AURORA_DEMO_STREAM=400,400,j2k=<folder>,net=200,size=3`), three alternated passes of the previous and the new behaviour in one binary: wait before the first pixels, weighted by the size on screen, 2.30 to 2.46 s → 0.73 to 0.75 s (2.25 → 1.83 s unweighted); requests 490 to 497 → 408; bytes 9.1 to 9.4 MB → 6.2 MB; pixels decoded 6.0 to 6.3 Mpx → 3.4 Mpx; every texture shown after 4.26 s → 3.46 to 3.96 s. What remains is the ceiling of 24 requests at a time (item 13). The `texture load:` line gains the wait before the first pixels of the downloaded textures, plain and weighted by their size on screen, and the first requests sent for a texture not seen yet. Tests: first range, level held by the bytes, first pixels, level for the size of the file, the pass keeping the size it saw, the asset server (requests, ranges, several requests on one connection). `check.ps1` green (1,885 tests passed, 24 ignored). Priorities between kinds of assets.** Every mesh was queued at 1e12, settings and landmarks at 1e12, materials and sounds at 9e11, animations at 8e11, textures at 1e5 at most plus their size on screen: on arrival the animations of the avatars, our own bakes and the sky waited for the whole mesh queue, far meshes included. Done (`aurora_net::Lane`, `scene/fetch_priority.rs`): two lanes. The urgent one goes first, ranked by kind: sky and water settings and a landmark a window waits on, then our own bakes (`/texture/<our agent>/` in the bake URL, Firestorm's `BOOST_AVATAR_BAKED_SELF`), interface images and what we wear (meshes worn by our avatar, HUDs), then animations, sounds, PBR materials. The bulk lane holds meshes and textures ranked together by their size on screen in pixels, what shows nothing yet first, a mesh before a texture of the same size (without its mesh an object is not there at all). Firestorm gives each kind its own connections (`LLAppCoreHttp::init_data`, llappcorehttp.cpp); here the lanes share the 24 slots: 4 kept for the urgent lane were tried and left out, since once its few requests were served they stayed idle and slowed the whole arrival by a sixth (15.1 → 17.5 s); an urgent request waits for the next slot to free up, a few milliseconds. Measured in demo with the new `AURORA_DEMO_ARRIVAL` (an arrival in a busy region: 1,200 objects all around, one in three a mesh, 16 avatars playing 32 animations, every asset downloaded from the local asset server, the avatar turning round after 3 s), alternated passes of `main` and the branch in one session: the 32 animations arrived after 0.67 s instead of 4.08 (200 ms a request), 0.25 s instead of 0.52 to 0.58 (70 ms).
