Late animations and landing-parcel data are observed for five seconds; an unclassified AO hover requires fresh finite physics, negligible vertical motion and 300 ms without actual foot support. A rail of eight sections, sampled every half second while the view shows, a minute of history: overview (processor, graphics card, memory, video memory, network and disk tiles, frame time breakdown, biggest consumer of each resource), subsystems (sortable table of the viewer's parts and sub-parts in seven columns, % of the machine or of one core, filter, detail pane with threads, related settings and the processor's minute), threads (per logical core load, the viewer's and the media plugins' processes, every thread group with its priority and role), memory (process, video memory against the driver's budget by kind, texture budget pressure, texture queues, GPU buffers written per frame), network (traffic, link figures, HTTP by kind, UDP throttle by channel, connected regions, busiest UDP messages), disk (reads and writes, cache by folder, hit rates, bytes by origin), scene (costliest avatars or objects, Inspect) and region (simulator health, time dilation, simulator frame). - 🟡 Windows Alt codes in every text field (human request, 2026-10-16): left Alt held, digits on the numpad, Alt released gives the character (Alt + 3 = ♥, Alt + 130 = é, Alt + 0128 = €). Windows sends it as a `WM_CHAR` after the Alt key-up, which winit 0.30 drops (it only attaches a `WM_CHAR` to the key press before it, `platform_impl/windows/keyboard.rs`), while egui-winit typed each digit held with Alt as text of its own. `alt_codes.rs` reads the sequence from the key events (`App::alt_code_key`) when egui has a text field focused: its digits are kept from the field, the character goes to egui's next frame. Windows' rules: no leading 0, the system's OEM code page with glyphs for 1 to 31 and 127 (437 in the United States, 850 in Western Europe); a leading 0, the ANSI code page (1252); numbers above 255 wrap around 256; 0, control characters and empty slots give nothing; on another system, or in the tests, 437 and 1252. Another key between the digits, or no digit, gives nothing; outside a text field Alt and the numpad keep their shortcuts; text a platform would attach to the Alt release is used instead of ours, never added to it. Unit tests of the composition and the tables, a UI test of a focused field receiving ♥ without the digit. Tried by the human with a real keyboard in demo on 2026-10-16. ⬜ upstream: winit should deliver that character (draft in the task's `.scratch/`).

Auto follows the system's regional format, read once at startup: Windows' short time (`GetLocaleInfoEx`, `LOCALE_SSHORTTIME`), LC_TIME's T_FMT on Linux (`newlocale`, `nl_langinfo_l`), 24 hours elsewhere; 12 hours write "3:07 PM" (AM / PM from the catalogues). Local time carries its zone's abbreviation ("14:07:12 CEST", CET in winter): the system's zone read once at startup (`iana-time-zone`, which maps Windows' zones to IANA names), its abbreviation from the embedded tz database (`chrono-tz`, about 1.3 MB of the release exe: every zone, the computer's being known at run time only), worked out once a minute so a daylight saving switch shows; where the database has only numbers ("+04") or the zone is unknown, the offset ("UTC+4", "UTC+5:45"). The island's tooltip and the Legacy bars' clock tooltip give SLT and local time with how far it is from SLT ("SLT +9 h") (`ui/bars/clock.rs`). SLT now follows the US daylight saving rule of the chat transcripts (`pacific_offset_hours`) instead of a day-of-year range. Difference with the Legacy Viewer: its status bar shows SLT alone, and FSStatusBarTimeFormat defaults to the format of the viewer's language (24 hours without seconds in English, with seconds in French), with 12 / 24 hours, seconds and time zone variants (LLStatusBar::updateClockDisplay); Aurora's Auto follows the system's regional format, the user's own 12 / 24 hours choice.

- 🟡 **Name tags and floating texts hidden by the scene, like Firestorm** (`aurora-render/src/label_depth.rs`, `shaders/labels.wgsl`, `ui/hud.rs`). Before: the names of everyone within the name tag distance were drawn over the image, through walls, roofs and floors. Firestorm draws the name tags and the floating texts in the world with the depth test (`LLHUDNameTag::render`, `LLHUDText::render`: `LLGLDepthTest gls_depth(GL_TRUE, GL_FALSE)`): a wall hides the names behind it and cuts the one of a resident standing half behind it. Same result here, for the plates, the classic name tags and the floating texts: the visible part of a label stays, the part behind the scene is not drawn.
  - **How**: the interface marks the point of the world each label stands at (`aurora_render::world_label_at`), and what it paints for the world is drawn by a pipeline of the renderer instead of egui-wgpu's: same vertices, textures and colours, each fragment compared with the depth of the scene at its pixel. The cut is smoothed over the four depth texels around the pixel and follows the jitter of TAA (it does not shimmer). No readback, no copy of the image, no wait.
  - **Where a name tag stands**: half a metre in front of its anchor above the head, toward the camera (`ui::hud::tag_point`), so that the avatar's own head, hair or hat never cut it. Deliberate difference from Firestorm, which pulls it by the radius of the whole avatar (`LLHUDNameTag::updateVisibility`) and so shows through a wall the name of someone standing a metre behind it. The floating texts keep Firestorm's point (pulled by the radius of their object).
  - **Not hidden**: the floating texts of our HUD attachments and the tracking beacon, as in Firestorm; transparent surfaces (glass, water) hide nothing, they are not in the depth.
  - **Cost**, in front of the demo crowd (`AURORA_DEMO_CROWD=40`, `AURORA_DEMO_POS="129,134"`, 42 name plates, 229 interface meshes, capped at 120 fps), five alternated passes against `AURORA_LABEL_OCCLUSION=0`, median of the `perf summary` lines: `r_egui` 0.16 ms versus 0.12 (the labels' vertices copied with their depth); `gpu=` 0.83 ms on both sides, `u_tags` 0.08 on both sides. Consecutive meshes with the same texture and clip share a draw (the depth is in the vertices).
  - **Clicks**: a click on a name tag reaches its avatar only where the tag shows (`App::pick_name_tag` compares the depth under the cursor with the same point).
  - **Demo**: `AURORA_DEMO_TAGS=wall` (the wall in front of two residents, a floating text behind it); `AURORA_LABEL_OCCLUSION=0` draws the labels over everything, by egui-wgpu, as before. The far residents of `AURORA_DEMO_TAGS` moved out from behind the plaza's torus, which now hides what is behind it.
  - 🟡 Validated by the human on Agni on 2026-10-13 in a short session (one region, half a minute, nothing to report). To complete on Agni: a crowd under a roof seen from above (no name through the roof); a resident half behind a wall or a door frame (the name cut along the edge, without shimmer when the camera moves, in TAA too); nobody's name cut by their own head, hair or hat; names seen through a window or water; a click on a half-hidden name tag (the avatar only where the tag shows); the classic name tags and the floating texts of objects behind a wall.

- 🟡 **Avatar name plates** (`ui/nameplate.rs`; mock-up chosen by the human: variant A, with the tight green halo of B) — coded, pre-validated in demo from screenshots on 2026-10-13, **not yet tried on the grid** (tests to do below). The name tag above an avatar becomes a glass plate with round ends: profile picture in a circle with a status dot, display name in semi-bold (Inter SemiBold with the embedded fonts), user name, group title, round badges floating on the upper right edge, light border and soft shadow. It is the only rounded surface of the interface (docs/BRANDING.md, AGENTS.md section 7).
  - **Three levels according to the distance to the camera** (constants of `nameplate.rs`): full plate up to 15 m, compact pill (name and badges on one line) up to 40 m, name alone beyond. A plate only changes level 1.5 m beyond a threshold and slides from one level to the other in 0.18 s (interpolated size, contents cross-faded). At most 8 full plates at a time, the nearest ones: in a crowd the following ones are compact (a full plate keeps its place as long as fewer than 10 avatars are nearer). "Name distance" and the fade beyond 40 m are those of the classic name tags. The size follows the previous one: display name at 13 points on the full plate (plate 50 points high), the rest by the proportions of the mock-up (secondary lines at 8.8 points, name at 11.1 then 9.6 points at the compact and distant levels).
  - **States, from `LLVOAvatar::idleUpdateNameTagText`** (llvoavatar.cpp): away → amber dot; do not disturb → red dot (it wins); otherwise green; blocked → plate at 62%, name dimmed in italics, forbidden badge, no dot; friend → green heart badge; typing (typing animation, never on our own plate, like FSShowTypingStateInNameTag) → badge with three animated dots; avatar too complex (shown as a silhouette) → triangle badge; in the voice channel → green microphone badge, out of it → no microphone badge (since 2026-10-14); speaking → green outline with the halo, at all levels; avatar still loading → thin bar under the text.
  - **What the classic name tag wrote, and where it went**: "(Away)" and "(Do Not Disturb)" → the dot; "(Blocked)" → the badge and the dimmed plate; complexity and surface area (options "Complexity in name tags", "Silhouettes only", "Mine too" unchanged) → one line of the full plate, or "· 245,000" after the user name when the group title takes the third line, in amber beyond the limit and in grey otherwise (Firestorm's gradient from green to red is no longer there); red struck-through microphone outside the voice channel → nothing (the human's choice of 2026-10-14, after a red badge had been tried the same day); green → orange → red outline according to the voice level → green outline and green halo that follows the level, only while the avatar speaks (human request of 2026-10-14: a silent participant has no outline, since the server does not tell whether someone's microphone is open, only their voice activity). At the compact and distant levels only the name is left (and the badges in compact): the group title, the user name and the complexity are not there.
  - **Name options unchanged** (display names, user name, "First Last" format, hide "Resident"): a hidden line is absent, never empty. A name that is too long ends with "…" at 191 points wide, on the plate only.
  - **Voice**: envelope specific to the plate (`VoiceEnvelope`: rise in 40 ms, fall in 280 ms, gate that turns the halo off in 220 ms at the end of speech); the speaking ring below (it replaced the halo of the mock-up's `.speak.thin` rule), drawn only around the plate, never under the glass; nothing in silence.
  - 🟡 **Voice states changed at the human's request (2026-10-14)**: the green outline only while the avatar speaks (the server's voice activity, `"v"` of the WebRTC data channel; it turns green and back with the halo's gate instead of switching), on every plate including ours; outside the voice channel no microphone badge at all: the red struck-through microphone first chosen that day was taken back by the human the same evening (`feat/nameplate-names-ring`), the classic name tags keep theirs. Demo `AURORA_DEMO_TAGS=voice`. Validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-14 (`AURORA_DEMO_TAGS=cycle`). To complete on Agni: a crowd (red microphone on the plates of everyone out of voice, compact pills included); in a voice parcel, the outline that appears when someone speaks and goes when they stop, without blinking between syllables; nobody's outline while silent but connected; our own plate (outline while we speak, red microphone with voice off in the preferences or on a parcel without voice).
  - 🟡 **Speaking ring (human request of 2026-10-16; validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-16 with a real microphone; to verify on Agni: other residents' levels (server "p"/128) reach amber/red only when they shout, our own plate the same as in demo)**: the halo became a ring around the plate whose gap, width, opacity and glow all grow with the smoothed level (`paint::loud_ring`, `paint::voice_light`), so the intensity reads at a glance: a whisper is a faint hairline hugging the plate with almost no glow, a normal voice a green ring a few points away over a soft glow, a shout a thick bright ring pushed out with a wide glow; it closes in on the plate as the voice starts, and is tighter around compact and far plates. The color is the microphone badge's green, sliding through `p.amber` to `p.danger` past the overdriven level like the Legacy Viewer's speaking indicator (LLVoiceClient::OVERDRIVEN_POWER_LEVEL, llvoicevisualizer.cpp, out of reach of WebRTC's levels): here a real shout, red from -18 dBFS of RMS over 300 ms to -12 (`nameplate::overdrive`, smoothed like the level), while normal speech, -30 to -24, stays green (the classic tag's -10 dBFS was never reached by a real shout). Same envelope (no flicker), palette colors only. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_VOICE=sweep` with `AURORA_DEMO_TAGS=voice` (Tess goes whisper → normal → shout → normal every 8 s, our plate on the real microphone, whose meter is turned into the voice server's scale); `AURORA_VOICE_LEVEL_LOG=1` logs our own plate's level once a second (demo or grid).

The match / mismatch pair stays the classic tags' own. A friend's heart badge is green (`heart-filled`, `success`; it was light violet); a violet ring around a friend's picture was tried the same day and dropped by the human; the status dot is unchanged (present, away, do not disturb). Settings from before the switch keep the colours by relation on if the classic tags were the style.

"Click on a plate" (`Settings::plate_click`: nothing by default, view profile, send IM, offer teleport, open the avatar menu — entries of the avatar's menu): over another avatar's plate the pointer becomes the hand of a clickable object, and a left click without Alt / Ctrl / Shift runs the action instead of reaching the world (`app/plate_click.rs`); the right click, Alt camera, HUDs and our own plate are unchanged. Demo `AURORA_DEMO_PLATE_HOVER=x,y[,click]`, `AURORA_DEMO_PLATE_CLICK`. Validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-14 (hover on pills and far names, with and without "full plates for friends only"; the four click actions and the hand cursor). To complete on Agni: hover and click in a crowd, the click actions on real residents, the Alt camera and HUD clicks over plates.
    - ⬜ Later: hover tests the plate's rectangle only, not the scene's depth (a plate hidden behind a wall can grow when the pointer passes over where it stands; the click does test the depth); more click actions already in the avatar's menu could be offered (Add friend, Teleport to avatar, Pay).

"Reduce animations" keeps the light and drops the bounce. Not in the Legacy Viewer.
  - **Deliberate difference from Firestorm, requested by the human: colours fixed by the theme.** The plates do not read the name tag colours of the preferences (configurable in Firestorm): name in `ink` (ours too), `violet_light` for a friend, `rose` for Linden Lab staff, `muted_dim` in italics for a blocked resident; user name `muted`, group title `teal`. These settings now only serve the classic name tags: on the Colors page their group is greyed out (without disappearing) with the note "Used by the classic name tags." as long as the Plate style is chosen; the minimap markers and the chat colours stay active. What the plate no longer shows: the "My name" colour, and the "Matches / Non-matches" distinction (two identical colours by default).
  - **Other differences, from Firestorm or from the mock-up**: typing is always shown (FSShowTypingStateInNameTag is off by default in Firestorm); the scene blur is darkened by 35% under the tint (`GLASS_SHADE`), without which the plate turns light grey on a white wall or a bright sky and its grey lines get lost in it; the badges are 90% opaque instead of 72% (they have no blur of their own, the plate's border would show through); no saturation of the blur (the windows' one, shared, as is); filled Tabler icons (microphone, heart, triangle, forbidden) instead of the mock-up's outline icons; blur reserved for the 16 nearest plates (full or compact), denser tint for the others and for the distant pills.
  - **Drawing and cost**: the geometry of a plate (pill, border, shadow, halo, picture ring, status dot, badge discs) is made of simple meshes (`nameplate/mesh.rs`) instead of egui's rounded shapes, kept as long as the avatar's state does not change, moved on every frame and redrawn without a copy when the plate has not moved (`nameplate/paint.rs`). Measurement: demo `AURORA_DEMO_CROWD=40` (41 name tags), dev build, cap at 120 fps, the two styles alternated every second in the same session (`AURORA_NAME_TAGS=alt`), medians of the 30 seconds of plates and of the 15 seconds of classic name tags of each pass, PC shared with other agents.
    - in the crowd (`AURORA_DEMO_POS=135,134`), camera still, 3 passes: `u_tags` 0.06 ms versus 0.05; `r_tessellate` 0.16 versus 0.14 to 0.15; `r_egui` 0.12 versus 0.09; 165 egui meshes versus 195; 18,000 vertices versus 13,200;
    - in front of the crowd (`129,134`), 2 passes: `u_tags` 0.08 versus 0.06; `r_tessellate` 0.16 to 0.17 versus 0.14 to 0.15; `r_egui` 0.12 versus 0.09; 162 meshes versus 195;
    - geometry copied again on every frame (upper bound of a moving camera, forced for the measurement), 2 passes: `u_tags` 0.11 versus 0.06;
    - worst frame: frame `max` identical (8.35 to 8.43 ms at the cap); `r_tessellate` exceeded 1 ms in 2 seconds out of 210 with the plates (1.14 and 1.24 ms), never in the 105 seconds of classic name tags;
    - first version, with egui's shapes and no limit on full plates: `u_tags` 0.22 ms, `r_tessellate` 0.33, 39,300 vertices.
  - **Demo**: `AURORA_DEMO_TAGS=voice|status|cycle` (nine residents in all the states, at the three distances, generated pictures, white wall behind two of them); `AURORA_NAME_TAGS=classic|plate|alt` to force a style or alternate during a measurement (docs/TESTING.md).
  - 🟡 To validate on Agni: real profile pictures (arrival delay, round cropping, residents without a picture); halo on real voice levels (amplitude, no flicker); legibility in a real crowd (thresholds of 15 and 40 m, limit of 8 full plates) and on a bright sky; away, do not disturb and typing of real residents; friends, blocked residents, Linden staff; names with extended characters in semi-bold (they go through the system fonts, in normal weight); right and left clicks on a plate; `u_tags`, `r_tessellate` and `r_egui` in a busy place.

- 🟡 **"Search" window (Firestorm's legacy search, Ctrl+F and button of the bottom bar)**: port of FSFloaterSearch and its panels (`fsfloatersearch.cpp`, `floater_fs_search.xml`, `panel_fs_search_legacy_*.xml`, flags of `llqueryflags.h`, `llclassifiedflags.cpp`, `lleventflags.h`, content access of `llagentaccess.cpp`). Tabs in the order of `floater_fs_search.xml`: Web, People, Groups, Places, Land Sales, Events, Classifieds; the window opens on the last tab used (FSLastSearchTab, 0 = Web the first time). Network (`aurora-net/src/search.rs`, `session_search.rs`): DirFindQuery (people, groups, events "u|category|text" or "day|category|text"), DirPlacesQuery (sorted by traffic), DirLandQuery, DirClassifiedQuery, sent reliably with the flags of `find()`; replies DirPeopleReply / DirGroupsReply / DirPlacesReply / DirEventsReply / DirClassifiedReply over UDP and DirLandReply through the event queue (with ProductSKU), ignored if they name another agent; details by AvatarProperties (AgentProfile capability, otherwise UDP), GroupProfileRequest, ParcelInfoRequest, ClassifiedInfoRequest, EventInfoRequest; land types by ProductInfoRequest. Model (`world/search.rs`): one list per tab, query identifier (a reply to an older query is ignored), pages of 100 (the row beyond announces the next page: "> 100 found"), status codes (banned word, terms too short, nothing found, search disabled, and those of the events), words of 2 letters or fewer removed (`filterShortWords`), UUID key typed in People resolved by the name cache, filters reapplied on the viewer side (price / area of the land, maturity rating of the events), first row selected and its details requested. Window (`ui/search.rs`, `ui/search/details.rs`): form of each tab (Firestorm's categories, G / M / A checkboxes, General / Moderate / Adult level of the groups, price ≤ and area ≥, sale type, server sort and ascending order, "Ongoing and Upcoming" or date with previous day / next day / today), list with sortable headers, counter, previous / next pages, details on the right with their actions (profile, IM, teleport offer, friend, block, map, name menu; group chat, copy of the URI and of the name; place profile of "Places" with Teleport, Map, Copy SLurl; classified sheet; event sheet with clickable organiser and place). Firestorm's default values: General content only (ShowPG* = 1), General groups (FSSearchGroupMaturity = 13), land sales like `FSPanelSearchLand::find`: "Price ≤" checkbox ticked and "Area ≥" checkbox unticked (FindLandPrice = 1, FindLandArea = 0), price field showing "0" and area field empty (the local source leaves `edit_price` empty, the released Firestorm shows 0 there; the query is the same, 0, and the 0 makes visible what is sent; an emptied field still counts as 0), type "All Categories" selected (FindLandType), sorted by name; DFQ_LIMIT_BY_PRICE / DFQ_LIMIT_BY_AREA follow the checkboxes, both values are always sent (0 for an empty field) and the viewer filters the replies again (price > limit or area < limit discarded): by default only the rows at 0 L$ remain, that is the auctions, displayed at 1.0 L$/m² as in Firestorm, the window closes after a teleport (FSLegacySearchActionOnTeleport = 1), last tab remembered (FSLastSearchTab). Deliberate differences: the M and A checkboxes are greyed out with an explanation when the account or the content preference does not give access to them (Firestorm leaves them tickable without sending them); next / previous page replays the query of the displayed page, even if the field was changed in the meantime; no drop-down history of searches. Web tab: the grid's search page in the built-in browser (CEF, `ui/web_view.rs`) with back, forward, reload, search page, editable address and "Open in browser"; the page is opened with the session, like Firestorm (`FSPanelSearchWeb::loadURL`, `LLWeb::expandURLSubstitutions`, `LLViewerMedia::getOpenIDCookie`): the address is Firestorm's `SearchURL` with `sid=<session id>` (the `[TYPE][COLLECTION]` tokens stay as they are in it and `&maturity=g|gm|gma&` is added, as its panel does), and the OpenID cookie of the login is given to the browser before the first page (it only goes to its own domain). The session identifier is only put in a `https://search.secondlife.com` address built by the viewer, is never logged or saved by Aurora, does not appear in the address field and "Open in browser" opens the address without it; the browser and its page are dropped on logout; nothing is sent in demo. The browser of this tab has its own profile (`media/private_profile.rs`): as the CEF plugin has no in-memory mode (it always gives CEF `<cache_path>cef_cache/<pid>` and a log file), its cache, its history, its local storage and its `cef.log` go into `cache\web-private\<pid>-<n>\`, **deleted after use** (closing the window, logout, exit of the viewer, and a sweep at the next start of what a crash left behind; a lock protects the profile of another running viewer); nothing of this page goes into the shared cache `cache\cef` nor into `cache\cef.log`. While the browser is running, these files exist on the disk. Deliberate differences: the page is only loaded when the Web tab is displayed (Firestorm loads it every time the window is opened); on the beta grid (human request) nothing of the session is sent — neither `sid` nor OpenID cookie —, the page of `search.secondlife.com` is opened anonymously there with the note "Web search is anonymous on this grid.", whereas Firestorm sends the beta's session identifier to the main grid's site. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_SEARCH=<tab>[:text]`, `AURORA_DEMO_SEARCH_WEB=<page>`; unit tests of the flags, messages, replies, pages, statuses and replies of the demo. **Nothing has been tried on the grid.**
  - **Shared theme**: the window passes the theme guard (`ui/theme_guard.rs`) with no exception or marker. G / M / A, "Price ≤", "Area ≥" and "Ascending" checkboxes through `widgets::checkbox`, "Ongoing and Upcoming" / "By Date" through `widgets::radio_value`, text only measured in `Color32::PLACEHOLDER`; sortable header, sort arrow and row highlight like the radar (`ui/people/radar.rs`); "More" menus through the rows of `ui/menu.rs`. The guard now also recognises an egui checkbox written on its own line of a call chain (`.checkbox(`) or without a label (`egui::Checkbox::without_text`), which it used to let through.
  - **Ctrl+F, a single rule** (`ui/find_shortcut.rs`, function `owner`, tested): three functions ask for it — the search of the script editor, the search bar of a conversation (Conversations and History windows) and "Search". 1) The keyboard is in a field: the window of that field wins (script editor, conversation), wherever the pointer is; 2) the keyboard is nowhere: the conversation under the pointer; 3) otherwise — nothing selected and pointer elsewhere, or keyboard in another field (chat bar, filter, field of "Search") — the viewer's shortcut on these keys, "Search" by default, like the accelerator of Firestorm's menu. The same rule is read by the window when it draws itself and by the application before launching its shortcut: never both, never neither. The shortcut of "Search" remains editable in the preferences; placed on other keys, it no longer yields anything.
  - **Windows**: `widgets::Floater`, so placed by a `Slot` of the layout like the others (follows the edges of the viewer's window, snaps to the other windows and to the work area, moves as a block with its neighbours); closed at the first launch; opened in the middle of the work area (`search::default_rect`, 900 × 600, minimum 720 × 440; Firestorm: 780 × 590, centred), away from the bars. At 1280 × 720 it lands at (190, 57) and leaves visible 182 px of the radar on the left and of Performance and Conversations on the right, the minimap almost whole (test `the_first_launch_windows_take_their_corners`).

Also: Ctrl+F on the real keyboard (keyboard in the field of a conversation or pointer over Conversations: search bar alone; pointer over the world or keyboard in the chat bar: Search; script editor: its search); `cache\web-private` folder empty after the Web tab is closed; on the beta grid, page opened anonymously.

The report shows a group title surrounded by "ღ" (Georgian, U+10E6); also missing were Armenian, Hebrew, Arabic, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, the Indic scripts, Thai, the mathematical letters of "fancy" names (bold, script, fraktur, double-struck), circled letters, arrows, box drawing and blocks, braille… These characters now come from the fonts installed on the system, as in Firestorm (`fonts.xml`, `<os name="Windows">` added to each font, looked up by `LLFontRegistry::createFont` in `LLFontGL::getFontPathSystem`; Firestorm additionally embeds DejaVu Sans, which draws its "ღ"). Aurora's own list: one Windows 10 / 11 font per script (Segoe UI, Segoe UI Symbol, Meiryo or Yu Gothic, Malgun Gothic, Microsoft YaHei and JhengHei, Nirmala UI, Leelawadee UI, Ebrima, Gadugi, Microsoft Himalaya, Javanese Text, Segoe UI Historic, SimSun-ExtB, Segoe UI Emoji for recent emojis in monochrome…), Japanese before Korean and Chinese like Firestorm, the first font present that has the probe character being kept. They come after all the embedded fonts, in both families: what was already drawn does not change. Files memory-mapped without a copy (no weight added to the package, no new dependency), looked up and checked on a separate thread from launch, installed on the next frame if they were not ready; baseline of the fallback fonts aligned with that of the main font (egui centres their line, which raised Japanese by a quarter of the font size). Module `ui/fonts/fallback.rs`. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_GLYPHS=1` (or `2`), comparison with `AURORA_FONT_FALLBACK=0`. Measurements (dev profile, this PC): lookup 1.3 ms off the main thread; construction of egui's fonts 1.3 ms instead of 0.2 to 0.4 ms, once; `ui` step unchanged (0.35 to 0.44 ms before and after); about 2.5 MB of resident memory at launch, 6 MB after displaying all the scripts of the demo. The fonts are now installed after the layout (`App::new`), test of the order in `ui/layout.rs`. `check.ps1` green (1,095 tests passed, 13 ignored).   - ⬜ later: right-to-left word order (bidi algorithm, absent from egui 0.36) and cursor / selection in these texts; combining marks taken from a font other than that of their base letter, which egui does not draw ("᭄" after Latin letters); colour emojis in name tags, lists and fields (Noto 3D only in messages); macOS and Linux font lists written but never tried (Windows releases only); embedded fallback font (DejaVu Sans like Firestorm, about 750 KB) if a system without these fonts has to be supported
  - ⬜ later, when egui is fixed (defect of egui 0.36.2, [emilk/egui#8576](https://github.com/emilk/egui/issues/8576), still present on its `main` branch; no fixed version as of 2026-10-12; egui 0.37.0 shapes mixed runs right ("a אבג b": 7 glyphs) and Ctrl+← from the end of "Aurora بღd" works, but an Arabic-only run still has surplus glyphs, "بب": 3): previous word in a field that contains letters written from right to left. Cause: a run that starts with a right-to-left letter and has n characters comes back from shaping with 2n − 1 glyphs ("بب": 3 glyphs), whatever the fonts, whereas all of egui's cursor code counts one glyph per character. The end of the line therefore goes past the text, and the "previous word" (`ccursor_previous_word`) subtracts below zero: Ctrl+← sends the cursor back to the start of the text, Ctrl+Backspace and Ctrl+W erase everything before the cursor instead of one word, a double-click after the last word of a field selects from the start (published and development builds); the "Debug" viewer and the `ci` profile (overflow checks) stop. No reliable workaround in Aurora alone: the number of glyphs is set in `epaint`, with no hook, and the viewer has about 75 input fields. The human's choice on 2026-10-12: wait for the upstream fix rather than embed a fork of egui; a fix in two small pieces (`epaint` and `egui`) was verified on a copy of egui 0.36.2 with `cargo test --profile ci` and proposed upstream ([emilk/egui#8698](https://github.com/emilk/egui/pull/8698), as a draft, to be reviewed by the human before marking it ready). Tests in `ui/fonts.rs`: `egui_still_shapes_surplus_glyphs_in_right_to_left_runs` fails as soon as a version of egui fixes the defect; the two `#[ignore]` tests that follow it will then have to be re-enabled, Ctrl+← and Ctrl+Backspace put back in `fallback_text_survives_selection_and_editing`, and the chat field and the script editor checked in demo
- 🟡 **Right-to-left text in reading order (bidi)** (human request of 2026-10-27): Arabic and Hebrew sentences were drawn with their words from left to right (egui 0.37 has no bidi algorithm; its shaper only reverses each run of one font), Arabic-Indic digits reversed. Module `ui/bidi.rs`: the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm (`unicode-bidi`, mirrored brackets with `unicode-bidi-mirroring`) on top of egui's layout. A text that holds a right-to-left letter or an Arabic-Indic digit is broken into rows first (own line breaking, `max_rows` and the overflow character kept: the end in reading order is cut), each row is put in display order (rules L1, L2, L4), and egui gets it with each right-to-left word in its own section in reading order (the shaper reverses and joins it) and each other right-to-left character alone; `Visual` keeps the box of every character of the original text for links, badges and selection. Other texts go through egui unchanged. Applied to the name tags and plates (names, titles), object and HUD floating text, chat bubbles above the avatars, the chat bar and its cards, and the Conversations transcript, where a message read from the right flows from the right edge (pieces, links and emoji pictures in reading order) and keeps drag-selection and copy in reading order. A chat line that starts with its sender's name stays left to right, the name isolated as between FSI and PDI (`Base::Sender`): it stays first, after its picture, and an Arabic message follows in its own order. The one-line labels cut with an ellipsis (`widgets::elided_label`, `paint_elided`: message headers, lists, tabs) go through `ui/bidi.rs` too, cut at their end in reading order, whole in their tooltip. Each character keeps its own direction for the cursor and the selection (Latin words in a Hebrew line), selected right-to-left text takes the selected text colour, and painting alone (name tags, floating text) skips the characters' boxes. Going beyond the Legacy Viewer, which has neither shaping nor bidi. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_GLYPHS=rtl`, `rtl2` (with `AURORA_DEMO_BARS=legacy AURORA_DEMO_CHAT_LINES=legacy`: the lines above the chat bar with their pictures). PR #1191, maintainer review addressed. Validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-27 (Linux); to verify on Agni with real names and chat.
  - ⬜ later: text fields (chat input, script editor, notecards) still show right-to-left text in memory order; notifications and group notices, and the labels of the interface not cut with `widgets::elided_label` or `paint_elided`, not yet through `ui/bidi.rs`; the position of a character inside a right-to-left word is shared evenly (selection and links inside a word are approximate)

Cause: egui lays a face's vertical shift (`fonts::optical_center_offset`, 0.59 px for Inter at 13 px, nearly half a pixel) out unrounded and epaint draws each glyph rounded to the pixel; the ink / baseline helpers measured the layout, and positions were rounded in points. `widgets::ink_rect` now rounds each glyph as epaint does, `galley_baseline` reads where the letters stand, positions go to the physical pixel, the badge is centred on the square epaint fills: badge, letter and capitals within half a pixel of each other with Inter, Noto Sans, Roboto and Segoe UI at 1, 1.25 and 1.5 (test `the_place_island_centres_its_badge_and_texts_with_every_font`). Same class elsewhere: text beside an icon centred by egui's text row stood up to 1.9 px from the icon, every font; `widgets::row_text_origin` puts the letters' optical middle on the row, used by the action buttons, menu rows, check boxes, radios, tabs, pills, keycaps, navigation, section headers, the system island's tooltip, People, Conversations, the chat bar and the windows' list rows; `paint_ink_left` (favourites, balance, place rights) no longer centres each line's own ink (a name with descenders stood 1.5 px higher); the segmented choice reads the capitals as drawn instead of three quarters of the ascent. Test `labels_are_centred_on_their_icons_with_every_font`: within half a pixel for every shared widget, font and scale. `AURORA_UI_FONT` / `AURORA_UI_SCALE` compare the fonts and scales without touching Preferences.

A window left smaller than its default size also gets its place back at startup: egui measures it on its first frame and then keeps it within the screen as if it had its default size, which pushed it away from the bottom and right edges (Conversations at the bottom right); the next frame puts it back where it was.   - 🟡 Snapping windows (human requests of 2026-10-12; `ui/snap.rs`, `ui/layout/gesture.rs`; Firestorm: LLView::findSnapRect / findSnapEdge, SnapEnabled, SnapMargin = 10 px, dependent floaters): a window moved by its title (the minimap: by its whole surface) to less than 10 px from the facing edge of another open window, of the top bar, of the bottom bar or of a screen edge sticks to it; next to a neighbour, its edges on the same side also align (top with top, etc.). Each axis chooses the nearest snap. It follows the pointer without jumping: a violet guide shows the edges that are going to touch or align and the outline of the place where it will land, and the snap happens on release; the guide does not flicker (the displayed snap holds 4 px beyond the margin, a neighbour must be clearly closer to replace it). **Resizing**: the dragged edge or edges snap to the same targets, under the pointer (the window is laid out again at each size and its content can refuse one: snapping on release would have caused a jump); a snap that would go below the minimum size is not offered. **Snapped windows**: two windows placed side by side by a snap (not by a mere alignment) stay together: dragging one moves the whole group, as one block, kept whole within the screen and snapped like a single window (each member against the other windows, the outline of the block against the bars and the edges); the group is saved with the layout and follows, as a block, the nearest edge when the viewer window changes size. A window leaves its group when it is closed, when it is collapsed, when the common edge is pulled apart by resizing it, or when it is dragged with **Alt**; Alt during a gesture also prevents any snap. During the gesture, a pill near the window is a reminder of it: Alt key then "do not snap" (snap offered) or "detach this window" (group), after 150 ms. Snapped windows touch, edge to edge, each other as well as the bars and the edges, like Firestorm's floaters (see the "no gap" sub-line). Aurora choices compared with Firestorm: a window attracts another one only if they would share a stretch of edge, guide and snap on release, groups for all windows. "Snap windows" setting (Preferences › Interface, enabled; `snap_windows`). All `widgets::Floater` windows and the minimap, which switches to the same resize handles as the others (`widgets::bare_window`). Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_SNAP=1|groupe|taille`. **To be tested by the human (does not depend on the grid):** the real mouse gestures, verified so far by tests and by the scripted demo only — move a window near another one, near the bars and the edges, drag an edge towards a target, move a snapped group, Alt during the gesture, move and resize the minimap.

The first-launch layout follows the same gap, so its four windows are also placed against the bars, the edges and their neighbour (Performance touches the minimap; at 1280 × 720, Conversations opens 284 px high instead of 252). Limit: a saved layout keeps its positions, and two windows snapped at 8 px by a previous version stay where they are but no longer form a group; snapping them again is enough (or "Reset everything").
    - ⬜ later: resizing the common edge of two snapped windows moves only that edge (the link is then removed); a splitter behaviour (the neighbour grows or shrinks by the same amount) remains to be done. Cancel land sale), acquisition, area, traffic (ParcelDwellRequest), Abandon / Reclaim, Buy a pass. **Rules**: estate, owner, covenant text (EstateCovenantRequest then the notecard by asset transfer from the estate), date, resale / subdivision. **Objects**: capacities, return of the objects of the owner / of the group / of others and of an owner in the list (Firestorm's confirmations), auto return, list of owners (ParcelObjectOwnersRequest, online = in our region, FIRE-1292). **Options**: rules of onCommitAny (group ticked automatically with "All", no pushing imposed by the region, scripts cannot be turned off in a damage area), search (128 m²), maturity, category, picture, landing point (Set / Clear / Teleport, FIRE-10043), teleport rules. **Media**: type (widgets from mime_types.xml), home page (MIME type by HEAD request), description, texture, scale, size, loop. **Sound**: music URL with the list of saved streams (FIRE-593, saved in the settings), local sounds, avatar sounds, voice, MOAP. **Access**: public, 18 years old, payment, group, pass, allowed / banned lists (adding through a resident picker: AvatarPickerSearch search, friends, nearby, UUID; ban duration), CSV export / import. **Experiences**: allowed / blocked lists (names by GetExperienceInfo), removal. **Environment**: Firestorm's unavailable cases, region settings (resetParcel), day length and offset (ExtEnvironment PUT on release), apparent time, sky altitudes. Group names by UUIDGroupNameRequest. Deliberate differences: pass price / duration sent as soon as they change (Firestorm, like LL, ties them by mistake to the group checkbox), refused stream removed from the list only for the parcel where it was chosen (FIRE-29157 also removed it when changing parcel), dates of the owners list in French SLT time (instead of RFC 1123), wider window for the 9 tabs. Demo: AURORA_DEMO_LAND=<tab>[:owner]. Validated by the human on 2026-10-09 ("Test a-propos-terrain"), tests on Agni still to do

Its text goes to the sender's transcript (log_to_im). Decline or close sends IM_LURE_DECLINED (lure_callback).

Yes offers a teleport as send_lures does (no text, our location SLURL) and writes the "Teleport offer sent" notice; No sends nothing (teleport_request_callback). Before: it landed in the nearby chat as "Name: text", and was lost without a text.

  - Deliberate difference: Firestorm shows nothing when our offer is declined or accepted (IM_LURE_DECLINED / IM_LURE_ACCEPTED end in its "unknown dialog" log). Aurora writes a system line, "<name> declined your teleport offer", in the conversation with that resident, or only in their transcript when none is open, instead of the former notification: the sender otherwise never learns the answer.
  - Each offer and request is a pending invitation with its answer (`TeleportInvites`); `World::answer_teleport_invite` answers it and closes its notification, ready for the card of part B2.

The textures in view load at full resolution (only while the texture budget is not under pressure), "Take" waits for them (at most 20 s, "Loading the details…" in the panel), and photos up to 3840 px are drawn at twice their size then reduced (supersampling). A setting the user changes in Preferences meanwhile is theirs and kept. The user's values are set aside (`Settings::photo_held`, never serialized) and are what a save writes in the meantime; they come back when the window closes or the switch goes off. ## Audio and voice

- ✅ Region voice restrictions ([#1247](https://github.com/Aurora-Viewer/Aurora-Viewer/issues/1247), PR #1261, 2026-10-28; task `voice-region-rules`; validated by the human and merge authorized on 2026-10-28): nearby voice now requires the current region's `ALLOW_VOICE` permission as well as the parcel's, following `LLWebRTCVoiceClient::voiceConnectionCoro`. The per-frame channel selection leaves an existing spatial session when permission is revoked and waits while region permissions are unknown; private/group/conference calls remain independent of spatial permissions. EN/FR status messages. Three regressions cover all region/parcel permission combinations on estate and parcel channels, missing permissions and hanging up a call on forbidden land.
  - ✅ Live parcel-property refresh: follow `LLViewerParcelMgr::processParcelProperties` when a selected/hovered parcel is the agent's current parcel in the same region. Confirmed replies now update the live voice/sound/fly/build/script/push flags, avatar limit fields, music/media and environment version as well as About Land. Keep the agent's parcel bitmap/bounds and notification sequence; reject no-data and obsolete agent notifications. Identical refreshes preserve live caches. Eight additional protocol/state regressions pass; `scripts/check.ps1` green: 5,970 passed, 30 ignored; formatting and Clippy clean. Region flags already refresh through SimStats.

Every volume slider goes through `widgets::volume_slider` (Preferences › Sound, the volume panel of the top bar, the media controls, a resident's voice row in their menus, the call strip and stage menus). With the option on, the knob moves along the cubic curve of PulseAudio's and ALSA's mixers (gain = position³: −18 dB at the middle, silence at the bottom, exact inverse); a resident's voice (0–200 %) keeps 100 % at the middle, its lower half on the curve. The stored values stay the linear gains of the Legacy Viewer (LLPanelVolumePulldown, LLSpeakerVolumeStorage, which has no such option): turning the option on or off moves the knobs, never the loudness; shown percentages stay the real gain. The import window's sound gain is an upload setting, not a playback volume, and keeps its linear slider. Also: the master row of Preferences › Sound › Volumes lines up with the channels' (it keeps the room of the enable box it lacks, the percentage sits in a fixed column; already misaligned on main, test `the_volume_sliders_line_up` at two UI scales and with OpenDyslexic). Demo `AURORA_PERCEPTUAL_VOLUME=0|1`.

The file is its FSStreamList setting as pretty LLSD XML (`stream_list.xml`, a map with the URLs under "audio" and "version" 1, `settings/stream_list.rs`), so files go both ways between the two viewers; `aurora_llsd::to_pretty_xml_string` ports LLSDXMLFormatter's pretty form byte for byte. The dialogs run off the frame (`app/stream_list.rs`); a notice tells the file written or the number of streams imported. Deliberate difference: a file that is not an LLSD map is refused with a notice, where the Legacy Viewer would replace its list with it (an empty list after a wrong pick); blank and repeated URLs are skipped, as the Sound tab's Add never saves them.

The history window ("Recently played"): newest first, Ctrl / Shift to choose, Copy to clipboard one title per line, Clear, Max. entries (0 to 10,000). Better than the Legacy Viewer: a long title slides smoothly instead of losing one letter at a time (same 4 s wait at its end), and a smaller maximum applies at once. Aurora addition (human request on #1124): a text-only look (the window's title bar button, `audio.stream_title_text_only`): the title alone over the world with a shadow, dragged anywhere, its place kept with the windows'; its right click opens the history, copies the title, gives the window back or closes it. Demo `AURORA_DEMO_STREAM_TITLE=[window|history|text][,stop]`.

## To explore

Open-source technologies that could set Aurora apart (human request of 2026-10-16). Not decided: each one needs a feasibility study first (Rust integration, size, cost per frame, licence). All the licences listed fit the GPLv3. Large models (translation, speech) cannot be embedded in the exe: they would be downloaded on demand when the option is turned on.

- ⬜ Noise suppression of the microphone with a neural filter (RNNoise, BSD; or DeepFilterNet, MIT / Apache 2.0): keyboard, fan and room echo removed far better than classic filters, at a small cost. First in the suggested order.
- ⬜ Better levels of detail for meshes, rigged avatars first, with meshoptimizer (MIT): simplification and vertex cache ordering, for more frames per second in crowds. First in the suggested order.
- ⬜ Local translation of nearby chat and IMs with Bergamot / Marian (MPL-2.0, the engine of Firefox Translations): on the PC, no API key, no message sent to an online service; one model of about 20 to 40 MB per language pair.
- ⬜ GPU-ready compressed textures in the cache (Basis Universal, Apache 2.0, or bc7enc, MIT): far less JPEG2000 decoding, faster loading, up to four times less video memory (see also the BC7 line of "Optimisation").
- ⬜ Captions of voice chat with whisper.cpp (MIT): other residents' voices transcribed on the PC, for deaf or hard-of-hearing residents and for muted sound; model of 75 to 150 MB, optional.
- ⬜ Spatial audio with Steam Audio (Apache 2.0): binaural 3D sound, occlusion by walls, room reverberation, for venues and nearby voice.
- 🟡 Ambient occlusion with Intel's XeGTAO (MIT): an option of Preferences › Graphics, see the GTAO line of "Rendering".
- 🟡 Visibility bitmask (Therrien et al., "Screen Space Indirect Lighting with Visibility Bitmask", 2023), after GTAO: a thickness per sample instead of XeGTAO's heuristic (thin objects, hair, railings occlude without darkening what is behind them), then screen-space indirect light from the same horizon search — done as Preferences › Graphics › Indirect light (GTAO), see the GTAO line of "Rendering"
- ⬜ God rays, decided for later by the human on 2026-10-17 (the Legacy Viewer has none):
  - first, screen-space light shafts: a radial blur from the sun's position on screen through the depth (GPU Gems 3, "Volumetric Light Scattering as a Post-Process"), about 0.1 to 0.3 ms, fading out when the sun leaves the frame
  - then possibly froxel volumetric lighting with the shadow cascades (Wronski 2014, Hillaire 2015), about 0.5 to 1.5 ms, to match with the SL sky's haze, water and transparent faces; it would open volumetric fog and projector beams later
- AMD FSR upscaling is already planned in "Rendering" (the upscaler chosen for Aurora).

- ✅ Saved files read by an older build (2026-10-14, validated by the human on 2026-10-14 on the strength of the tests and of a demo run on a settings file from a newer build, with nothing visible to test): a value the build does not understand (a shortcut added later, a new enum variant, a field whose type changed) made the whole `settings.json` fall back to the defaults, and the next save erased the file. `tolerant.rs` reads strictly first, then removes only the value `serde_path_to_error` names (an object entry, a list element; a required field or a fixed tuple climbs to its container) and reads again: unknown fields are ignored, lists keep their valid elements, one log line per value left out (its path, never its value). `settings.json` from a newer version (higher `settings_version`) runs no migration and is written back over the newer file: keys this build does not know stay, values it could not read stay while unchanged here, and the newer version number is kept. Any repaired or unreadable file is first copied to `<name>.newer-backup.json`. Applied to `settings.json`, `login_accounts.json` (shown without the unreadable entries, never rewritten while they are there, as an unreadable catalogue already was), `hud_scales.json` and the skin's `theme.json` / `layout.json`. Tests: a settings file from a newer build (unknown option, enum variant and shortcut, version + 5) keeps the rest and loses nothing over two saves; a damaged value in a current file; an account, a HUD size and a theme value from a newer build.

- ✅ Automatic crash reports (issue #688, human request of 2026-10-22; the four steps below are merged, open checks in their sub-lines): through GitHub only, with no server of our own; the minidump and the log stay on the tester's PC. The issue is created in the tester's name, then a repository workflow symbolizes and deduplicates it.
  - ✅ Module + offset stacks and the public summary (task `crash-report-summary`, validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-22: crash window unchanged, `public-report.md` checked; nothing to test on the grid): the native exception filter and the panic hook write each frame as `module+0xoffset`, with each module's PDB identity (CodeView GUID and age, code id) read from its PE headers in memory, without loader lock or symbol engine. `crash/summary.rs` builds the public text (`public-report.md` in the session folder): version, commit, crash kind, exit code, duration, system, GPU, the stack from the fault, the modules, the panic location reduced to a path inside the sources, and the closed log vocabulary (`crash/privacy.rs`, moved from the disabled form). Raw addresses, panic messages, paths and log lines are never copied.
  - ✅ Symbol files (task `release-symbols`, no effect on the viewer; dry run of 2026-10-22: 56 MB `.sym`, 6 MB zip): the Windows job of the Release workflow converts the release build's PDB with `dump_syms` 2.3.9 into `Aurora-Viewer-vX.Y.Z-windows-x64-symbols.zip` (store layout `aurora_viewer.pdb/<debug id>/aurora_viewer.sym`), published with the release; a pull request that changes the workflow now runs the Windows job as a dry run too and keeps the file as an artifact. Checked locally on the dev build: the report's debug id matches the symbol file and its offsets resolve to the right functions and lines.
    - ⬜ At the next release: check that the symbols zip is published and that a crash of the published exe resolves with it.
  - ✅ Triage workflow (task `crash-triage`, no effect on the viewer): `.github/workflows/crash-triage.yml` runs `scripts/crash-triage.ps1` on each new issue carrying the `aurora-crash v1` marker. It downloads the symbols of the report's release (debug id checked), resolves the viewer's frames with inlined functions to functions and source lines, appends them with a signature (crash kind + first three meaningful frames by stable name), then closes the issue as a duplicate of the first open issue with the same signature, with an occurrence comment there, or renames it `Crash: <kind> in <function>` with the Bug type. No label: the signature is a hidden comment. Fixture tests in `scripts/test-crash-triage.ps1`, run by the workflow on pull requests; a local mode reads a `public-report.md`. Checked on real demo crash reports: 2 s for a 60 MB symbol file.
    - ⬜ First real crash issue: check the triage on GitHub (symbols download, title, type, duplicate closing).
  - ✅ Sending from the crash window (task `crash-report-send`, validated by the human on 2026-10-22: the demo flow with the simulated GitHub, then a real authorization and a real issue created from a killed session's window): "Send a crash report" shows the issue to publish (the session's public summary, preceded by an optional "What were you doing?"), then "Connect to GitHub" (the GitHub App's Device Flow, `crash/github.rs`) and "Publish on GitHub", or "Open in the browser". The authorization stays in the system credential store through `keyring` (an expiring user token and its refresh token, refreshed without client secret and replaced at each refresh); "Forget the GitHub connection" in the window and in Preferences › Privacy. Preferences › Privacy › Crash reports: Ask (default; the Legacy Viewer always sends, to its own server, while this is a public issue in the tester's name), Always (sent when the window opens, once authorized), Never (no send button). `sent.txt` prevents a second sending; no label, no upload, no `api.auroraviewer.com`. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_CRASH_SEND` with a simulated GitHub.
    - ⬜ Later: the disabled bug report form (`bug_report/github.rs`) can reuse `crash/github.rs` when it comes back. Its picture and private log uploads are removed since the 2026-10-22 cleanup: direct sending publishes the text only and the tester drags the saved picture into the issue.

- ✅ Windows between the bars (validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-13; was "the Performance window covers the right of the bottom bar when it is open", and Performance in full view, About Land and the bug report over the bottom bar at 720 to 900 px high). Requested by the human on 2026-10-13: a window must never cover the top bar or the bottom bar, it passes behind them, and its title bar must never leave the interface, where it could not be taken back. In `widgets::Floater`, for every window: it is kept in the work area (`layout::work_area`, the screen without the bars) instead of the screen, and paints and takes the pointer there only, so what would stick out is behind the bars; it opens no larger than that room and inside it (default size, minimum size and default position brought into it); a window as tall as its content (fixed or of automatic height: Performance) whose content is taller than the room scrolls its body, and takes its own height again when the content fits; a resizable window left larger than the room (viewer window made smaller) is brought down to it, as `LLFloaterView::adjustToFitScreen` does; and whatever places a window (layout, placement, resize, drag of one larger than the room, which egui lets slide out title first), its title bar is put back in the room at each frame, whole in height and by 96 px at least in width. The worn HUDs are drawn before the interface (`renderer.rs`: world labels, HUD attachments, then the rest), so the bars already cover them. Tests: positions kept in the room, content taller than the room, windows sent outside or larger than the room, clip at the bars. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_PERF=full` at 1280 × 720, `AURORA_DEMO_LAND=objects` at 1280 × 720, `AURORA_DEMO_BUG_REPORT=1` at 1600 × 900.
  - ⬜ Later: the list context menus that go down over the bottom bar at 720 px high; the mini-map (`bare_window`, dragged by its whole surface) is still kept in the screen, not between the bars; a HUD positioned over a bar is covered by it but not moved.
  - 🟡 Windows over the whole screen with the islands (human request, 2026-10-16: the islands leave room between them, above and below, that the windows could not use). With Aurora's islands a window is moved anywhere on the screen (`layout::move_area`, set with the work area in `App`; the work area stays what windows open in and snap to). Each of the left, right and bottom edges stops the windows or lets them cross (Preferences › Interface, "Windows stop at the screen edges", `Settings::windows_stop_left / right / bottom`, all on by default: a window stays whole on the screen): past a side 96 points of its title bar stay on screen, past the bottom its whole title bar; never above the top (`layout::reach`, given to `constrain_to` and to the drag of the gestures). The top has no setting: a title bar above it could not be grabbed, so letting it open would allow nothing more. Islands and windows share a layer (the last clicked comes on top), so a title bar hidden by islands all but its grip comes out of them once the button is released: below the top row, above the bottom one (`layout::clear_of_islands`; the islands report their rects, `layout::island_drawn`). A saved place from another layout or a smaller screen is brought back by the same rules (`keep_title_in`). With the Legacy Viewer's full-width bars the windows stay between them (no room to win), the same edge settings applying. Toolstrips move over the whole screen too; a group of glued windows stays whole on it. Demo: `AURORA_DEMO_WINDOWS=reach-top|reach-bottom|reach-right|reach-left|reach-down` and `AURORA_DEMO_WINDOW_EDGES`. Unit tests of the reach for each edge open or closed, the uncovered width and the way out of the islands. Validated by the human in demo on 2026-10-16 (gaps of the bars, each edge with the settings on and off, a title dropped on a top island); no "top" setting, by the human's choice: a title bar never goes above the screen.

What was still left at the old place was the agent's position, see "Our position while seated on an object" in "Controls". To verify on Agni with that line: a seat without a seat camera (rear view behind the seated avatar), one with a seat camera, a vehicle.

## Transparent picking and hover — PR #212

- ✅ Build inspector ownership status (human request, 2026-10-19): keep the owner first for editable, non-modifiable and locked selections; show another owner's resolved avatar/group name, and use “Non modifiable” in French. Follow `LLSelectMgr::selectGetOwner` for common versus multiple owners. Full checks green: 3,890 passed, 26 ignored; formatting and Clippy clean. Regressions cover name lookup without cached properties, group and multiple owners, and actual header placement for own/foreign selections in every permission state. Three French native captures inspected. Validated by the human in the test viewer on 2026-10-19; merge authorized.

- ✅ Blend hover (13/10): left and right clicks validated by the human; hover now stops at foreground Blend geometry at every opacity, even without a click action. The media hover shares the cached surface point; candidate bounds, per-face modes and large-face triangle hierarchies are retained. Mask holes remain pass-through. Full checks before integration: 1,795 passed, 23 ignored, Clippy green; sequential tests after three render-thread timing failures in parallel, all passing in isolation. Tests cover the cursor, the point bounding media hover, cache reuse, mixed materials and overrides on omitted faces. Demo `blend-zero/faint/half/solid-ready`: prim 976 without an action, Default cursor with no bitmap; before, Buy 971 was announced behind zero-alpha Blend. `mask-zero-ready` reaches Buy 971 with its bitmap. The pointer is held on target for the frame-650 sample; AURORA_HOVER_CHECK reported no difference. Human validation and merge authorization on 13/10/2026. Checks after integration with the updated main: 1,808 passed, 23 ignored, fmt and Clippy green.

- ✅ Left click on Blend (13/10): Blend triangles stop the press at every texel opacity, including zero, even without an action. Parallel candidate search resolves the material mode per face, so Blend elsewhere on a mixed-material object cannot fill a Mask hole. GPU picking retains zero-alpha Blend texels and the existing Mask threshold; posed surfaces also block media, avatar and action fallbacks behind them. This priority was requested by the human, unlike Firestorm's preference for a visible interactive object behind a non-actionable transparent surface. Full checks: 1,795 passed, 23 ignored; TE, PBR, legacy materials, zero alpha, occlusion, mixed faces and omitted-face overrides. Demo `blend-zero/faint/half/solid` reaches panel 976 without opening Buy 971; `mask-zero` still opens Buy. No GPU error in the inspected captures; zero-alpha Blend measured 8.34 ms per frame before / after in the small scene capped at 120 fps. Transparent right click, invisible selection, IGNORE and linked Sit rechecked. Clicks and hover validated by the human on 13/10.

- ✅ Transparent object selection (13/10): right click and left click in edit mode include transparent surfaces without a Touch handler or click action, as LLToolPie::handleRightMouseDown / LLToolSelectRect::handleMouseDown with pick_transparent. Only candidate triangles are tested, in parallel; displayed depth still occludes CPU geometry, IGNORE is traversed outside build mode and selectable in edit mode. Objects with no drawn faces remain indexed when CPU geometry exists. Checks: 1,792 passed, 23 ignored, Clippy green; TE / texture / PBR / legacy, sky, range, occlusion and overlapping bounds. Demo `transparent-menu/build` and `invisible-menu/build`: prim 976 selected in all four cases, instead of the object behind. Captures inspected with no GPU error; 120 fps retained (8.33–8.34 ms per frame). IGNORE, Disabled and linked Sit rechecked. Left / right clicks and hover validated by the human on 13/10.

- ✅ Build inspector proposal (2026-10-16): port the interactive prototype to the native viewer: vertical coordinate modes, title permission states, shared rez-under-land-group option, separate linked-prim navigation, numeric increment buttons, inline material options, and preview-above-folder resource pickers with Inventory/Local/Aurora Library. Lists use resource icons and request only the selected preview. Normalize whole-object highlighting after confirmed reparenting. `check.ps1` green: 3,061 passed, 24 ignored, formatting/Clippy clean. Native FR captures of Materials and texture/material pickers inspected; normal-mode viewer launched as `Test build-interface-proposal online` from build 926b04ca. Validated by the human on 2026-10-16; merge authorized.
  - ✅ Compact resource picker (human request, 2026-10-16): reduce the default width by one third, from 480 to 320 points, and increase the default height from 600 to 720 points, within the available work area. Texture and material pickers share the portrait layout, a taller inventory list, two rows of preset buttons (Default/Blank above Transparent/None) and a full UUID field below them. Adopt the new default once for saved layouts, then retain subsequent manual resizing. The layout regression covers long names, empty inventories, material controls, font scaling, stable dimensions and reopening after a resize; reserve the initial footer before measuring it so scaled controls cannot grow a reopened window.
